News.title: Woman & her dog mauled in Rottweiler attack as they walked along popular UK beach as cops release CCTV in hunt for man
News.content:
DOG ATTACK Woman & her dog mauled in Rottweiler attack as they walked along popular UK beach as cops release CCTV in hunt for man

A WOMAN and her small dog have allegedly been attacked by a Rottweiler as they walked on a popular UK beach.

The horror incident, which occurred in Heacham, Norfolk, on Sunday, July 12, left the little pooch injured.

Police say the woman and her Lhasa Apso were approached by a Rottweiler as they walked on the beach at around 3:30pm.

The larger dog is then said to have mauled the small Lhasa Apso in a brutal assault.





Following the attack the little dog was left with a puncture wound near the spine and the woman was knocked over but not injured.

Police are now probing the incident and are appealing for any witnesses to come forward.

Norfolk Constabulary has released images of a man they want to speak to in connection with their investigation.

The force said: “Anyone who recognises the man or who witnessed the incident is asked to get in touch via the following channels quoting reference 36/51302/26.”

News.title: Teenage girl grabbed & sexually assaulted in field in broad daylight attack as cops hunt man
News.content:
ATTACK PROBE Teenage girl grabbed & sexually assaulted in field in broad daylight attack as cops hunt man

A TEENAGE girl has allegedly been grabbed and sexually assaulted in a broad daylight attack, as cops launch a manhunt.

The horror is said to have occurred in St Leonards, Sussex, at around 3pm on Monday.

A man approached the young girl in a field near Edinburgh Road before sexually assaulting her by touching, cops said.

The man is then alleged to have fled the scene towards Filsham Road.





Police have launched a probe into the horror and are appealing for any information that may assist them in their investigation.

The suspect is described as white, between 5’ 9” and 5’11”, aged between 25 and 35 with light brown curly hair and stubble.

He was reportedly wearing a red jacket and dark blue jeans at the time of the incident.

Detective Inspector Barry Chandler said: “This is a fast moving investigation and our specially trained officers are supporting the victim.



“We are appealing for any witnesses who were in the area who may have seen anyone of this description acting suspiciously or saw the incident to come forward.

“We would also like to hear from anyone with relevant CCTV or doorbell footage which could help our investigation.

“We are aware of the alarm that this will cause to the local community, and we have stepped up police patrols who will remain in the area while we continue to investigate. Please speak to our officers if you have any concerns.”

News.title: Mystery as goth influencer, 30, and boyfriend shot dead with their bodies found on rural road after being held captive
News.content:
SAVAGE END Mystery as goth influencer, 30, and boyfriend shot dead with their bodies found on rural road after being held captive

A GOTH influencer and her boyfriend have been shot dead as cops say they may have been held captive for drug debts.

Ulissias Marcelli, 30, and her partner Vinícius Souza de Carvalho, 28, were found with gunshot wounds on a roadside in Porto Seguro, northeast Brazil.



The pair had been dead for around a day when they were discovered on the rural road by a farmer on Friday night.

Cops have now launched a probe into the mystery killing – with initial leads suggesting the pair may have had ties with local drug cartels.



Officers told Brazilian newspaper G1 that the former beauty queen and her boyfriend may have been held captive before they were gunned down.

Cops added that they were investigating alleged debt linked to drug trafficking or to a possible sale of narcotics.

Forensic teams recovered seven spent bullet casings and seized Ulissia’s phone for analysis – that of her partner’s was missing.

No suspects have been announced and the motive for the murder has not yet been established.

The self-proclaimed “Miss Tattoo” was a fire dancer who posted content about rock music, motorcycles and animal welfare to her more than 20,000 followers.

Ulissias also leaves behind a 13-year-old son.



Both Ulissias and her boyfriend lived locally and worked in events catering.

The beauty queen’s mother shared her grief, writing: “Go in peace, my loves. You leave an immortal legacy. We will miss you dearly – this is such a heartbreaking loss.”

Ulissias won a local beauty title in 2021 and had been announced as a presenter at Rock Gaya Festival on July 25 – just days before her brutal murder.



The music and arts event posted a tribute to Instagram, writing: “On Thursday, we joyfully shared that Ulissias would be part of the Rock Gaya Festival as one of our presenters. Today, with profound sadness, we say goodbye to her presence among us.

“We are still trying to find words for a moment like this. It’s hard to believe that someone who was about to share such a special moment with us has left us so soon.”

Fans have shared an outpouring of grief on social media.

One wrote: “My deepest condolences to the whole family and to the son.”

“Brazil is experiencing rampant violence; my condolences to the family members”, added another.



The police have not yet arrested any suspects.

News.title: Boy, 15, charged with raping and sexually assaulting eight girls aged between 10 and 15
News.content:
RAPE PROBE Boy, 15, charged with raping and sexually assaulting eight girls aged between 10 and 15

A 15-YEAR-old boy has been charged with raping and sexually assaulting eight girls between the ages of 10 and 15.

The teenager, who cannot be named because of his age, allegedly committed the offences between 2023 and 2025.



He was charged with numerous offences including raping a girl under 13, making an indecent photograph or pseudo-photograph of a child, and sexual assault.

District Judge Amar Mehta told the boy: “Your case is too serious to be tried in this court.



“Therefore it’s going to be tried at the Crown Court at Northampton.

“I’m going to send your case to Northampton Crown Court for another hearing similar to this one.”



The teen was accompanied by his mother to Wellingborough Youth Court on Tuesday.

He was not asked to enter the dock and took a seat at the back of the court room.

The boy was charged with 22 offences related to rape and sexual assault against eight victims who were aged between 10 and 15 at the time.

He was not asked to enter any pleas during the 20-minute hearing.



The court heard he was being charged with 12 counts of sexually assaulting a female, three counts of assaulting a girl under 13 by touching, and one count of raping a girl under 13.

As well, he is facing charges of one count of assaulting a female aged 13 and over by penetration with a part of the body or thing, one count of raping a girl aged 13-15, and two counts of making an indecent photograph or pseudo-photograph of a child.

He is also being charged with possessing a prohibited image of a child and another of possessing extreme pornographic images.

Following the decision by District Judge Mehta to have the boy tried at a crown court, he will next appear on August 18.

The judge granted him a conditional bail, instructing him not to contact the alleged victims.



He was also told to have no unsupervised contact with females under 16 and to engage with the Northamptonshire Youth Justice Service.

During the hearing, the boy spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address, and to ask the judge what the Youth Justice Service was.

News.title: Watch as defiant drivers flout warnings to cross COLLAPSED bridge
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment a car crossed a river, using a buckled bridge in Greece to save 20 minutes on their commute.

Footage shows the vehicle on the out-of-service link – its midpoint only a few inches above Pineios River in central Greece.



Three years after Storm Daniel tore through the country, as well as Turkey and Bulgaria, Palaiopyrgos Bridge in Larissa remains heavily damaged.

The bridge once linked coastal communities in the municipalities of Agia and Tempe, but its collapse has disrupted local travel.



While considered unsafe, drivers continue to take the risk to avoid taking another, 19-mile longer route using the national highway.

Yiannis Beritzas, the president of the Paleopyrgos village, said the bridge has cut off direct routes to Mount Kissavos.

“What should we do? Should we go all the way around?” one local told Skai.

“Where should we go? Nothing can be done. We play with death every day.”

The situation becomes even more dangerous when the level of the Pinios River rises and the waters pass over the crumbled bridge.

The Palaiopyrgos Bridge is among the infrastructure that has not been repaired yet.



Although the contract for the construction of a new bridge has already been signed by a well-known construction group, the project has not yet started.

“All traffic is at risk,” said the president of the Paleopyrgos Agricultural Cooperative, Thanos Hatzizogidis.

“Let’s not find ourselves running behind the events again. Large and loaded vehicles are passing by, while there is not even the necessary traffic lights.”



The catastrophic floods caused by the storm in 2023 resulted in around $2.14 billion worth of damage.

In Greece, 17 people died because of the storm, which at the time was described as a “biblical catastrophe”.

Five people were also killed in Turkey during the floods, while at least two victims were found in Bulgaria.

News.title: PC Andrew Harper’s killers ‘set for early release’ under Labour scheme as his mum furious over ‘insult beyond words’
News.content:
TWO of PC Andrew Harper’s killers could be set for an early release from jail under Labour plans to tackle prison overcrowding, with his furious mother branding it an “insult beyond words”.

Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were jailed for 13 years in 2020 for the manslaughter of the 28-year-old officer.



The pair, who were 17 at the time of the offense in August 2019, were passengers in the car that dragged PC Harper for more than a mile along country roads when his ankles got caught in a towrope loop.

He had gone to investigate the theft of a quad bike when Bowers and Cole tried to escape in a vehicle driven by a third killer, Henry Long.



PC Harper sustained serious injuries and died in the road.

But the pair are now eligible to be freed just halfway through their sentences under the Ministry of Justice early release scheme.

Debbie Adlam, the police officer’s mother, was told that his killers may have their sentences reduced in a letter from the MoJ.

The heartbroken mother told The Telegraph that the potential early release of the killers was an “insult beyond anything able to be put into words”.

She told the outlet: “It makes me feel sick. Andrew’s life doesn’t get to come back. It feels like a slap in the face and an insult.

“People are getting a free pass for crime in this country. I like to try to be proud of my country, but this isn’t something to be proud of. There’s a lot going wrong.”



It is unclear precisely when Bowers and Cole will become eligible for release, though it could be by the end of the year.

The driver, Long, is not eligible for early release under the scheme and will only be able to seek parole after serving half of his 16-year jail sentence.

The original sentences handed to the trio sparked a national outcry and a campaign for “Harper’s Law”, which introduced a mandatory life sentence for anyone convicted of killing emergency workers while committing a crime.



Led by the officer’s widow, Lissie Harper – who had married him just one month before his death – the campaign was backed by Labour at the time, alongside Tory amendments to enact the legislation.

Frontbenchers Nick Thomas-Symonds and Sarah Jones, now the policing minister, previously met Mrs Harper to offer their support.

The killers’ eligibility for early release will fuel fresh demands for Andy Burnham’s new government to rethink the controversial policy.



Under the scheme, serious criminals – including killers, rapists, and child groomers – are eligible to be freed halfway through their sentences rather than two-thirds, provided they have not committed serious prison rule breaches.

Criminals convicted of less serious offences can be freed as little as a third of the way through.

The scheme is written into law via the 2026 Sentencing Act and is expected to become operational this September, leading to the early release of more than 5,000 offenders over the following 10 months.

Before Mr Burnham became Prime Minister on Monday, sources confirmed he was reviewing whether and how to exempt rapists and child groomers in the face of a growing backlash.

An MoJ spokesman said: “This was a horrific crime, and our deepest sympathies are with Pc Andrew Harper’s family and friends.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“In 2024, the country was facing a prison crisis and a total breakdown of law and order, with judges ordered to stop jailing dangerous criminals.

“This government is committed to public safety: we are building prison places at the fastest rate since the Victorian era, and taking the difficult decisions needed to lock up the most dangerous offenders.”

News.title: Trump will allow Andrew Tate to be extradited to UK after self-proclaimed misogynist ‘raped & choked women unconscious’
News.content:
TATE PROBE Trump will allow Andrew Tate to be extradited to UK after self-proclaimed misogynist ‘raped & choked women unconscious’

DONALD Trump will allow the Tate brothers to be extradited to the UK to face sexual abuse and child pornography charges.

Self-proclaimed misogynist Andrew Tate has been accused of raping and choking women unconscious in Britain and possessing child abuse images.



British detectives demanded the arrests of the suspected rapists after a further four alleged victims came forward in the UK, bringing the total to seven.

The pair were detained in Miami on Saturday as they arrived at a bare-knuckle boxing event.



The Tate brothers’ lawyer Joe McBride slammed the arrests and claimed the duo were victims of a “political witch-hunt”.

He called on Trump to intervene and told reporters outside court that “he was elected to fight against this kind of nonsense”.



Andrew has previously said: “I’m very close with the Trump family. I know them well.”

The brothers had allegedly contacted people close to the president after they were detained – but the White House on Tuesday confirmed they would not step in.

A US Official told The Telegraph: “The White House has no involvement and no feelings on the issue.”

Andrew Tate has previously boasted of his high-powered connections in the US government – claiming that he befriended Trump’s son Barron in July 2024 after an assassination attempt on the president.



And the Financial Times reported that one of Trump’s top envoys had helped him and his brother flee Romania after their arrest last year.

When asked about this bombshell claim, Trump said: “I know nothing about that.”

The brothers, who are dual British-US citizens, face a total of 59 charges in the UK, according to Bedfordshire Police.



The allegations date from between 2010 and 2017 and include rape and sex trafficking.

Andrew faces 32 new charges, including seven relating to rape and 19 involving extreme pornography and indecent images of children.

Tristan, 38, faces six more, including two rape and sex-trafficking charges.

According to unsealed documents, Andrew allegedly repeatedly choked one woman until she passed out and then raped her at her home in Bedford in 2015.

Another woman alleged Andrew visited her Manchester home before choking her to the point that “she was afraid Tate was going to kill her”.



The complaint also alleged that Tristan regularly choked, beat and raped a woman that he was in a romantic relationship in 2012 and 2013.

Both brothers, who are dual US-British citizens, have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Tates were born in the US before moving to Luton as children.



They are now based in Romania, where they were first arrested in 2022.

News.title: Andy Burnham slashes bus fares to £2 across England as new PM makes ‘breathing room’ pledge to hard-up voters
News.content:
BUS fares will be capped at £2 across England from next year, Andy Burnham has announced.

The new PM lowered the current £3 ceiling as part of a cost of living package to give the public more “breathing room”.



As Manchester Mayor he capped fares on his flagship Bee Network to £2 for a single adult fare.

The cap was first brought in nationally at £2 by the Tory government in 2023 but was then raised to £3 in 2024.



The new cap will come in from January.

Mr Burnham has vowed to take “immediate” action to lighten the load on hard-up families before setting out real action at the autumn Budget.



He has admitted his first measures “won’t solve everything” but would be a start on the cost of living.

On Monday, he told his Cabinet that they needed to be a “cost of living government” as he set out his priorities.

As part of his cost-cutting initiative, he has also pledged to slash taxes on electricity bills from October.

With VAT expected to be taken off electricity bills, UK households would see £45 off their annual price cap.



Reducing the tax from 5 per cent to 0 per cent is another move by Mr Burnham to help bring down inflation.

He has said that the policy, costing £850million in 2026/27, will be paid off by cancelling the Digital ID cards scheme.

Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey MP said: “For too long, too many people have struggled with the cost of living.

“Today’s energy tax cut will give families some breathing room on bills, and provide some reassurance this winter.

“This measure is funded this year from cancelling the Digital ID programme, and it will help bring down inflation while supporting households in every postcode.”



But according to Starmer ally, Darren Jones, the Digital ID programme was “unfunded”.

Just after leaving Downing Street from his position as Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, Mr Jones posted online saying: “Good news that VAT will be cut on electricity bills.

“It’s a simple way for families to save a few quid, and to mechanically help to keep inflation that little bit lower.

“But the DigitalID program was unfunded.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The government will have to set out how it will pay for its new policies at the budget.”



It was not clear where the money to fund the Digital ID programme would come from In the Office for Budget Responsibility’s Economic and Fiscal Outlook from November last year.

News.title: Prince George has 'balance of tradition and family values' as he reaches major milestone
News.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales are working in tandem to prepare Prince George - who turns 13 today - with "a balance of tradition and family values" at the heart of his upbringing, royal sources have said.

As the young prince reaches his teenage milestone, the future king is taking another important step toward his destiny.

Sources close to the Prince and Princess of Wales have told how George has been raised with "an acute awareness of the constitutional role he will eventually occupy, but also with a determination from his parents that he should enjoy as normal and grounded a childhood as possible".

Long before George was born on July 22, 2013, the prince and princess have been united in preparing their first born, not only as a future monarch, but also to foster an appreciation for his or her role within their immediate family.

‌



Ingrid Seward, editor in chief of Majesty Magazine and respected royal author, said: "William and Catherine's duty as parents has never been solely to educate George - or any of their three children - about constitutional duty or public appearances.

“Their shared ambition has been to raise a young boy who understands both the extraordinary privilege of his birth and the ordinary values that underpin a happy family life.

“It is a balance that reflects their own contrasting childhoods and one they have consciously sought to blend for the next generation."

View 4 Images Prince George reaches a major milestone today, celebrating his 13th birthday (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

‌



Contrast of Prince William and Prince George's upbringings

Prince William's own upbringing was unlike that of any previous heir.

While his mother, Diana, Princess of Wales, sought to expose him and Prince Harry to life beyond palace walls, William's childhood was shaped by the pressures of monarchy, relentless public attention and the eventual breakdown of his parents' marriage.

Diana's death when William was just 15 and his brother Prince Harry fundamentally altered their adolescence and, by William's own admission, left an enduring impact on how he would later approach fatherhood.

The Princess, by contrast, was raised in a close-knit, loving middle-class family in Berkshire. This has shaped the very fabric of how she has approached her role as a mother, particularly her duty to George's upbringing.

‌



The princess’ parents, Carole and Michael Middleton, created a stable home life centred on family meals, holidays, sporting activities and strong relationships with grandparents and siblings.

It was an upbringing that offered consistency, emotional security and a sense of normality that would become one of Kate's greatest strengths as a parent.

Friends of the couple have long said that William admired the warmth and stability of the Middleton family long before they married.

Yet, despite his own at times turbulent relationship with his father during childhood, William enjoys a close relationship with the King as does all his children who especially love spending time with him during the summer holidays and at Christmas.

‌



As parents themselves, William and Kate have deliberately drawn upon their individual experiences, combining the Princess's emphasis on family life with William's unique understanding of royal duty.

In recent months George has accompanied his father on visits to The Passage homelessness charity and his mother to RAF Coningsby in Lincolnshire to mark Armed Forces Day.

View 4 Images George has been slowly introduced to royal duties, most recently visiting RAF Coningsby with the Princess of Wales to mark Armed Forces Day

George's public appearances are carefully managed

Aside from the worldwide media frenzy in preparation for his birth in the summer of 2013, George has been born into a world which has much more appreciation for the pressures on younger members of the royal family.

‌



Sources close to the family also point to the childhood that George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis have all been permitted to enjoy as a result, which is hugely different from previous royal generations. Both the Prince and Princess make sure they do the school runs, attend sporting fixtures, and enjoy regular family holidays in Norfolk and Scotland. Their time spent with the Middleton family has also formed a huge part of their upbringing, designed to provide routine rather than privilege.

At the same time, George has gradually been introduced to the responsibilities that accompany his place in the line of succession.

His public appearances have been carefully managed, increasing only as he has grown older. Whether attending Trooping the Colour, major national commemorations, Christmas at Sandringham or accompanying his parents to significant sporting occasions, such as Wimbledon earlier this month.

View 4 Images Prince George accompanied his mum and dad, the Prince and Princess of Wales, to the Wimbledon Championships, alongside sister Princess Charlotte (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire)

‌



George's education

Behind the scenes, William has taken a particularly active role in explaining the institution to his eldest son.

Ms Seward explained: "George's upbringing has been a perfect blend of appreciation for the tradition of the institution into which he was born and will one day lead, and respect for his own family life."

Education has also formed a central part of that preparation.

This autumn, George will begin secondary school life at Eton College, following in his father's footsteps almost three decades after William enrolled there in 1995.

‌



The decision carries obvious historical symbolism, but the decision for George to go to Eton was not one made solely by his parents or any senior courtiers within the institution.

It was a joint decision, between George, William and Kate for a multitude of reasons.

Like William before him, George will receive an education that has prepared generations of national leaders, while remaining close enough to the Waleses’ family home, Forest Lodge in Windsor.

George is understood to have enrolled in boarding at Eton but being so close to his family, is expected to take the opportunity to return home at weekends.

‌



View 4 Images George will start at Eton College this September, the same school his father Prince William attended as a 13-year-old in 1995 (Image: Getty Images)

'George shows all the qualities of his upbringing'

Another source close to the family said: “George is not only a delightful young man, he shows all the qualities of his upbringing. He is kind, caring and considerate and genuinely interested in the work his parents do within the institution.”

The source points to the significant role the young prince took on during last year's commemorations for the 80th anniversary of VE Day, where he sat for hours talking to war heroes about their experiences with incredible interest.

As George enters his teenage years, the careful balancing of matching his adolescence and role as a future king will continue.

‌



His profile will inevitably increase as he moves closer to adulthood, but his parents appear determined that public duty should never come at the expense of family life.

Jennie Bond, former BBC royal correspondent, said: “It’s obviously a huge year ahead for George. Becoming a teenager is still a ‘thing’ and quite a landmark in any young life.

“But when it means you are also moving schools and essentially leaving home – at least on a part-time basis – it’s pretty momentous.

“Luckily, George has two very switched-on parents who have brought him up to talk about his feelings and his fears, and they will only have taken the decision for him to start boarding at Eton after discussing it with him fully, and being certain that this is what he wants. So he’ll probably view the year ahead with a few nerves but a lot of excitement.

‌



“I’m sure he has a full understanding by now of what lies ahead – especially having seen the funeral of his great grandmother and the Coronation of his grandfather. It must be a daunting prospect - and hard for a young lad to realise that his destiny, his career and his life are mapped out already.”

The monarchy he will one day inherit will almost certainly look different from the one his great-grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, presided over for seven decades.

Yet the values the Prince and Princess of Wales hope to instil - service, humility, empathy and a strong sense of family - will prove just as important as any constitutional lesson.

News.title: EasyJet flight to Ibiza issues 'emergency code' and returns to Gatwick minutes after take-off
News.content:
EasyJet flight to Ibiza issues 'emergency code' and returns to Gatwick minutes after take-off

The flight has arrived safely at Gatwick, according to tracking data, but it is not clear why the plane performed a U-turn over the Channel and returned to its origin airport

View 2 Images The U-turn easyJet flight EZY52LD performed on Wednesday, July 22

A flight from London Gatwick to Ibiza turned around just moments after take-off for a ‘general emergency’ this morning.

‌



Wednesday’s (July 22) 5:35am easyJet flight to the Spanish island on Wednesday morning has now returned and landed safely back at London Gatwick, according to Flight Radar 24.

‌



It’s thought the plane transmitted a ‘general emergency’ code ahead of returning to its original airport. Eyewitnesses have said on social media that 'lots of fire trucks' are in attendance at the airport.

‌



“EasyJet Flight EZY52LD turns back toward London Gatwick Airport in UK after transmitting code 7700, indicating general emergency, shortly after takeoff,” Flight Radar 24 said.

View 2 Images An Easyjet plane [file image] (Image: Jam Press)

Data from the tracking software shows the aircraft took off from the airport in West Sussex, flew south towards mainland Europe, and then performed a U-turn over the Channel, before making it back to Britain's second-busiest airport.

‌



The aeroplane model involved is an Airbus A320-214. The cause of the emergency transmission has not yet been revealed.

However, the 7700 ‘squawk’ code is only used for ‘a serious situation requiring immediate assistance’ according to the Wayman Flight School.

The EZY52LD operates on a daily basis during the summer from Gatwick to Ibiza, and has been operating on schedule and as normal for the last week, data shows.

‌



The budget airline recently announced a new Spanish route from Gatwick. Flights have started to Reus, the Catalan birthplace of the legendary architect Antoni Gaudí, known for designing Barcelona's iconic Sagrada Família.

Kevin Doyle, easyJet UK Country Manager, said: “The addition of these popular Spanish destinations, Reus and Ibiza, to our networks and Holidays Portfolio from London Gatwick and London Southend provides our customers with even more choice and great value when booking their European holidays next summer.

"As the UK’s largest airline, we’re always aiming to make travel easy, providing great value to Europe’s most loved destinations, and we can’t wait to welcome more customers on board.”

Article continues below

Gatwick Airport and easyJet have been contacted for comment.

News.title: 'I learnt CPR at work and saved my dad's life two weeks later'
News.content:
'I learnt CPR at work and saved my dad's life two weeks later'

Her 54-year-old dad suffered a heart attack just as he was about to start gardening at home

View 7 Images Douaa gave her father life-saving CPR (Collect/PA Real Life)

A woman who saved her father’s life with CPR after his sudden cardiac arrest aged 52 said she had learnt the skill two weeks earlier at a workplace first aid course, which she signed up for to “impress” her manager in a new job. Douaa Sultan, 24, an insurance broker living in Bedfordshire, rushed outside when her father, Hussam, 54, a banking executive, suffered a heart attack just before he was about to shovel soil in his front garden on Sunday September 1, 2024.

‌



Their neighbour was already on the scene and on the phone to emergency services, when Douaa said she was “overtaken by adrenaline” and started performing her newly-acquired CPR skill. Within 25 minutes of Hussam’s cardiac arrest, three ambulances and one helicopter arrived to take over his urgent medical care, and he was taken to hospital.

‌



Hussam was put into an induced coma. He woke up on Tuesday September 3 to discover he had a broken rib from the CPR and a head injury from hitting the ground when he collapsed. He said his memory of this time is “very weak” but when he found out what his daughter had done to keep him alive, he said he was “deeply grateful” for her “bravery”.

‌



View 7 Images Israa, Hussam, Douaa and Boutaina (Daniel Lewis Photo/PA Real Life)

Hussam told PA Real Life: “I’m sharing this (story) as an appreciation to (Douaa) for what she’s gone through. I’m deeply grateful to her for her bravery… and to St John Ambulance for what they do for humanity.”

‌



Douaa started a new job in insurance at the start of summer 2024 when she was “fresh out of university” and said she wanted to “gain more skills” to “impress” her manager. When the opportunity to do a St John Ambulance first aid training course came up, she said she was initially “hesitant” because the office already seemed to have some first aid trainers.

At the insistence of her line manager – who was “very encouraging” – Douaa said she signed up and did the two-day course in mid-August 2024. Douaa said she learned “how to wrap bandages if anyone was to break a bone” to try to stop any bleeding, and the acronym DR ABC – meaning checking for danger, try to get a response, then check airways, breathing and circulation – as well as how to perform CPR.

View 7 Images Douaa encouraged others to 

‌



Douaa said: “I remember very vividly at the end of the training, my trainer at the time goes, ‘I hope you’ll never have to use the CPR, but it’s good to have’.”

Two weeks later, on Sunday September 1, Hussam said he went to the gym early that morning but skipped breakfast, and remembered he pushed himself “hard” and it was a “very hot” day. Hussam said he remembers looking down at the heart rate tracker on the treadmill and seeing that his heart rate reached 169 beats per minute.

‌



For a man of 52, this exceeds the maximum recommended heart rate of 168, according to the British Heart Foundation’s calculator. On the drive home, Hussam stopped to pick up breakfast for his family and some landscaping supplies, dropped them at home and then went outside to begin some landscaping work.

View 7 Images Hussam said he was ‘well supported’ by his family (Daniel Lewis Photo/PA Real Life)

‌



Hussam said: “The last thing I remember is closing the door behind me… then that’s it.” A neighbour spotted Hussam dropping to the floor, ran over, called emergency services and shouted for help.

Douaa said she and her mother “very distinctively” heard someone screaming for help, but they assumed it might just be a child who had fallen off their bike. She said: “So then we go out to the front door, and it’s my dad on the floor, and our neighbour with him.

“I think I was just completely overtaken by adrenaline and I didn’t feel anything… but I locked in. “You’re face down over the body, and you know what you have to do. It’s hard, and it’s even harder when it’s your dad,” she said.

‌



Douaa said she remembers “begging the ambulance to please hurry” and that time felt “very distorted”, but she “just kept going” with the chest compressions. At one point, she heard the sound of her dad’s ribs cracking, which she said was “horrible” but she knew she had to “do whatever it takes to try and save a life”.

View 7 Images Douaa did her first aid training in mid-August (Daniel Lewis Photo/PA Real Life)

‌



When three ambulances and a helicopter arrived within 25 minutes of Hussam’s cardiac arrest, they took over his life-saving care and Douaa said she “walked away to the side and had a little cry”.

Hussam was taken to hospital, where Douaa said there were “very difficult conversations” because they did not know what his state would be when he woke up. Douaa said: “It very much depended on how well I performed the CPR because that would have determined how much oxygen remained in the bloodstream to get to the brain.”

According to the British Heart Foundation, fewer than one in 10 people in the UK survive an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Hussam said he was put in an “induced sleep”, and when he woke, the “biggest relief”, Douaa said, was her father being able to answer questions like what the year was and when his anniversary was, because it meant his cognitive function was intact.

‌



View 7 Images Hussam is ‘deeply grateful’ to his daughter (Collect/PA Real Life)

“That was a big moment,” she added. After an MRI and a full check-up, Hussam was discharged from hospital 11 days after arriving and said he was “well supported” by his wife, Boutaina, as well as Douaa and his younger daughter, Israa, 22.

‌



Hussam learnt that his family history means that he is “high risk” of heart issues, as his father and older brother both needed cardiac operations in their 50s – even though he regularly went to the gym, is not diabetic, and does not smoke or drink alcohol.

He was encouraged to change his diet, reduce stress, and drink more water. Six months after her husband’s cardiac arrest, Boutaina did first aid training too. Douaa said: “It’s a skill that you have for life. I want everyone to go and sign up… because how often do you do first aid training and then actually save a life?”

View 7 Images A St John Ambulance trainer presented Douaa with her certificate after completing her training (Daniel Lewis Photo/PA Real Life)

Article continues below

Hussam said he was “deeply grateful” to his daughter for saving his life, adding: “I recognise how lucky I was and I’m grateful. Every time I see an ambulance, even if I’m in the car by myself, I salute them, because these people save lives.”

Nominations for St John Ambulance’s Lifesavers at Work Awards are open until Friday, September 4. To find out more and to nominate a first aid hero in your life, visit their website: h ttps://shop.sja.org.uk/pages/lifesavers-at-work-awards-nomination-form.

News.title: Delivery driver sacked after 30 years for stopping at KFC during lunch break
News.content:
Delivery driver sacked after 30 years for stopping at KFC during lunch break

The formal postal service worker lost his bid to get his job back after he swung by KFC in his work vehicle - he appealed against his dismissal to Australia's Fair Work Commission

View 3 Images File image, KFC (Image: Getty Images)

A postal service worker has lost his final bid to get his job back after he was sacked for swinging by KFC on his lunch break in his delivery van. The worker, from Newcastle, Australia, had worked for Australia Post for more than three decades before he was fired last year. He took the sacking to Australia's Fair Work Commission, claiming his dismissal was harsh and unreasonable. Alas, Fair Work did not rule in his favour. The Fair Work Commission found that Australia Post was justified in firing the man, despite his long service record with the national postal service, citing several major misconduct incidents on top of the KFC incident.

The KFC incident took place on May 7, 2025. Fair Work heard the postie had swung by the fast food eatery in his delivery vehicle without permission from his supervisor while on an unauthorised hour-long break.

View 3 Images The Colonel himself with some of his signature drummies (Image: Getty Images)

He had been allotted a 30-minute unpaid lunch break at 10.40am. Documents did not say the time of his unauthorised lunch break, but as per Commission deputy president Tony Saunders: "[He] was required to let his supervisor know if he was taking a lunch break at a different time or location." To make matters worse, that very same day the postie also left work 30 minutes early without permission. When the man was asked where he had been on this occasion, his supervisior claimed he was rude in response. At first, the man refused to speak, before telling his supervisor he had to go 'make an appointment'. The supervisor then questioned: "Why are you trying to be...." but then was apparently interrupted by the seemingly disgruntled postie, who offered "Evasive?" His supervisor agreed, describing it as the "perfect word". Australia Post told the Fair Work Commission the postie had also told the supervisor he planned to retire soon so he planned to "have some fun for the next two years". The national postal service alleged that that fun involved "playing games" with Australia Post as well as and ignoring his superiors and supervisors. In just one month, the man managed to rack up an eye watering nine unexplained absences. He also ignored 17 messages from his managers. "He said he thought the text messages might have been a scam, but ...[he] could not give a satisfactory explanation as to why he did not simply call his workplace to check whether the text messages were genuine," Mr Saunders said. It is unknown why these weren't dismissed by the Fair Work Commission, as Australian law has protected workers from adverse actions like dismissal or demotions such as this since August 26, 2024, under the nation's Right to Disconnect laws, which allow employees to refuse to engage with employers outside their designated shift times in some circumstances. The Commission deputy president found that while the worker may struggle to find another job given his age and long employment with Australia Post, the postal service was justified in firing him due to the "grave nature" of his misconduct.

View 3 Images It is unlikely that KFC will ever taste quite the same again for one Australian man (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

"A meaningful employment relationship cannot exist when an employee demonstrates an ongoing failure and refusal to co-operate with their employer," Mr Saunders said. The man also presented medical certificates to Fair Work which showed he had been diagnosed with an "acute stress reaction" due to interactions with his employer. Australia Post claimed it had responded to the diagnosis by reducing the his workload and time pressure. Ultimately, the Fair Work Commission ruled in favour of Australia Post - the company has since stated that it welcomes the ruling by Australia's Fair Work Commission.

News.title: Police issue update after man, 25, dies at campsite near Royal Welsh Show
News.content:
Police issue update after man, 25, dies at campsite near Royal Welsh Show

Three men were arrested following the death of Dewi Aeron Evans at a campsite during the agricultural event - police have now issued an update on the investigation

View 2 Images Dewi Evans died in a medical emergency at the Royal Welsh Show (Image: Dyfed-Powys Police)

Police have issued an update on their investigation into the death of a man at campsite near the Royal Welsh Show.

On July 18 police swarmed a caravan park near the Royal Welsh Show site following the death of a 25-year-old man after suffering what emergency services described as a "medical emergency".

Dyfed-Powys Police were called to Penmaenau Farm, Llanelwedd, following reports of a medical emergency. Despite the efforts of paramedics, the man died at the scene.

View 2 Images The caravan park near the agricultural show (Image: BBC)

Chief Superintendent Steve Davies said: “This is a tragic incident, and our thoughts remain with the young man’s family at this difficult time. I would like to reassure the public that this is an isolated incident, and the death is currently being treated as unexplained.

“There is no evidence of any ongoing risk to the wider public in connection with this sad incident.”

The young man has now been identified as Dewi Aeron Evans from Llanfihangel Glyn Myfyr, Corwen. The family have now paid tribute to their son, brother and grandson.

In a tribute shares by police, his family said: "Dewi Aeron Evans, a beloved and dear son, brother and grandson; will be a huge loss to the family and community in Uwchaled. The family and community would appreciate privacy at this difficult time.”

In an update on Tuesday, Dyfed-Powys Police confirmed the three men had been released from custody on conditional bail while enquiries continue.

The 2026 Royal Welsh Show runs from Monday, July 20 to Thursday, July 23, held at the official Royal Welsh Showground in Llanelwedd, Builth Wells, Powys. The four-day event is one of the largest agricultural shows in Europe.

Despite the incident, the site remained open for the 2026 Royal Welsh Show. A statement from a spokesperson for the show reads: "We are deeply saddened by this tragic news, and our thoughts are with the young man’s family and friends, and with everyone affected by this incident.

"We will continue to support Dyfed-Powys Police as their enquiries continue.The safety and wellbeing of everyone attending the event remains our priority.

Article continues below

"We are working closely as members of the Builth Wells Event Safety Group, which has extensive measures in place, including welfare and support services, medical provision and safety initiatives. We want everyone attending to feel supported and to have a safe and enjoyable time."

News.title: 'World's worst mother' let husband rape daughter, 11, and get her pregnant - then forced child to give birth at home
News.content:
'World's worst mother' let husband rape daughter, 11, and get her pregnant - then forced child to give birth at home

WARNING DISTRESSING CONTENT: The mother of an 11-year-old who was raped and impregnated by her husband faces multiple life sentences in 'the most serious sexual abuse' cases Oklahoma has seen

View 2 Images Cherie Walker now faces a life behind bars (Image: Muskogee County Sheriff’s Department)

The ‘world’s worst mother’ faces life in jail after allowing her husband to rape and impregnate their 11-year-old daughter.

‌



Cherie Walker, from Oklahoma in the US, faces multiple life sentences having been convicted of enabling husband Dustin Walker’s sexual abuse, reports the Daily Mail.

‌



She was also convicted of six counts of child neglect after authorities discovered the 11-year-old gave birth in the ‘deplorable’ conditions she and her four siblings grew up in at their Muskogee home, where they were raised without clothes and alongside dog faeces.

‌



Cherie Walker, 34, knew that her husband Dustin, 35, was abusing their 11-year-old daughter but failed to step in, prosecutors said.

“It's very emotional to realise that a child at the age of 10 and 11 was having sex with their stepfather, that she became pregnant and no one took her to the doctor and she gave birth at home,” Assistant District Attorney Janet Hutson said after the couple were arrested in August 2025.

“When you complicate that with the severe deplorable, uninhabitable conditions of that home, to know that's where she gave birth, where those children lived, without even the ability to get a drink of water in the middle of the night.

‌



“It affected everyone in law enforcement. It affected the investigators, it affected everyone who touched this case. It certainly affected me.”

The horrendous abuse was only discovered when the girl went to hospital after giving birth to her stepfather’s baby, and a DNA test found Dustin was the dad with ‘99 percent certainty’, according to news outlet KRJH.

View 2 Images Dustin Walker, 34, admitted the horrific abuse last week (Image: Muskogee County Sheriff’s Department)

‌



Last month, Dustin Walker was sentenced for his crimes. He apologised for his abuse in court.

Dustin entered what is known as a 'blind' guilty plea to six counts of child neglect and one count of sexual abuse of a child under 12 four months ago, in March. A blind plea means the defendant admits guilt for the crimes, and does not have a plea deal, meaning the Judge decides their sentence alone.

In his case, the Judge handed Dustin Walker a jail term of 42 years in prison, plus a life sentence, for abuse and neglect of a child.

Article continues below

Cherie Walker will be sentenced at a later date having been found guilty last Friday.

Another adult present in the home, Cherie’s mother Michelle Justus, will also go on trial on Thursday (July 23), accused of child neglect.

News.title: Heartbreaking question girl, 3, asked after being bitten by snake under Amazon package
News.content:
Heartbreaking question girl, 3, asked after being bitten by snake under Amazon package

Addy, three, was bitten by a Southern Pacific rattlesnake at their home in Santa Clarita, California and spent two days in a pediatric intensive care unit after antivenom treatment

View 3 Images Addy, three, was rushed to hospital after the horror snake bite (Image: GoFundMe)

The dad of a three-year-old girl who was bitten by a venomous snake hiding under an Amazon parcel has described the "terrifying experience".

Manuel Barajas' daughter, Addy, was bitten by a Southern Pacific rattlesnake at their home in Santa Clarita, California as she went outside to collect a gift that had been delivered in an Amazon package. Barajas said his little girl noticed a package containing a gift for her and rushed outside to collect it.

As Addy picked up the package a Southern Pacific rattlesnake that was hiding under the brown padded envelope bit Addy's left hand. Addy's mother, Lynn, immediately rushed her daughter to nearby first responders in a supermarket car park, who transported her to a hospital where she was given antivenom.

View 3 Images Manuel and his daughter Addy (Image: GoFundMe)

Gran who became national hero after foiling £100k jewellery heist has died aged 85 READ MORE :

Addy spent two nights in a pediatric intensive care unit where she received two additional rounds of antivenom treatment. Thankfully, she has since made a strong recovery. Speaking to KTLA, Barajas said: "She's doing great now.

"I'd say she's about 70 percent recovered. She's still bruised on her left hand where she was bitten.Her spirits are high, her demeanor is great, but she keeps asking why she got bitten by a snake."

Barajas said he was out of town on business when the incident occurred and rushed home to be with his family. However, he is now seeking support as the family faces significant medical bills from Addy's hospital stay, antivenom treatments, and time in the pediatric ICU.

Barajas also missed about a week's worth of work while caring for his family after the horror snake attack.

View 3 Images Addy, was bitten by the venomous snake (Image: GoFundMe)

Barajas wrote on GoFundMe page: "I’m reaching out for help after a terrifying experience that turned our world upside down." He added: "We are doing everything we can to support Addy's healing, but the costs are overwhelming. We never imagined we'd be in this situation, and it's hard to ask for help, but we need support to get through this difficult time."

At the time of reporting, the GoFundMe campaign had raised more than $13,8000 from hundreds of donors.

You can donate to the GoFundMe page by clicking here.

News.title: UK supermarkets face food shortages as Met Office issues heatwave verdict
News.content:
UK supermarkets face food shortages as Met Office issues heatwave verdict

Farmers are warning the next 10 days are crucial for the harvest - and British supermarkets' ability to stock key food later this year - as the UK teeters on the edge of drought

View 3 Images Food shortages have been seen in the UK after extreme weather before (Image: Getty Images)

Farmers are warning the next 10 days are crucial to prevent food shortages later in the year.

‌



Extreme hot weather has baked Britain dry this summer and seriously affected crops, agricultural experts say. The UK has had just 3 per cent of its typical July rainfall in 2026 — but the south and east of England have had no rainfall at all this month.

‌



Now, farmers are particularly worried about this year’s harvest, telling The Independent the weather in the next 10 days will be crucial in determining if there are food shortages later in the year.

‌



A National Farmers Union (NFU) spokesperson said: “Some areas haven’t harvested yet so what happens over the next week to 10 days could have an impact. We’re asking the Environment Agency to be flexible when it comes to abstraction.”

Dry weather means only 13pc of Britain’s rivers are at their expected levels. In East Anglia, water levels are so low farmers have had to stop taking water from rivers to grow crops.

It is shaping up to be a difficult harvest, Paul Tompkins, NFU deputy president, said: “Parts of the country, particularly in the east and south, have seen exceptionally low rainfall, creating real challenges for farm businesses.

‌



“For many arable farmers, this could be another difficult and expensive harvest after extreme weather in both 2024 and 2025 which saw both drought and flood.”

View 3 Images Fires have broken out on moorland across England

The National Drought Group says ‘prolonged dry weather’, the stage before drought, has been declared in eight regions. They are East Anglia, West Midlands, Devon, Cornwall & Isles of Scilly, Lincolnshire & Northamptonshire, Hertfordshire & London, Wessex, Thames, Solent & the South Downs.

‌



A hosepipe ban will come into effect for millions of Brits later this week, with customers supplied by Affinity Water, Anglian Water, Cambridge Water, Southern Water, South East Water, Thames Water and South West Water all told to curb their water usage, which surges by 30pc on hot days.

The extreme weather also means combine harvesters are at greater risk of catching fire during harvest season, potentially further exacerbating food shortages as crops burn.

Fires have scorched the UK this summer as it experienced three heatwaves, with a high of 37C recorded in Norfolk in late June.

‌



View 3 Images Some areas in the UK will reach higher temperatures than the majority of Greece (Image: WXCharts)

Weather maps show that temperatures are set to rise again next week, with high of up to 37C.

The Met Office has issued its long range weather forecast for August, offering insight as to whether another heatwave will grip the UK.

‌



According to the agency, temperatures during the period of 4 to 18 August “will very likely remain above normal, with potential for further hot spells, particularly in the south.”

The government has recorded 53 wildfires at Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), including the long-running moorland blaze at Dovestone and Tintwistle in the Peak District.

Rain is forecast this weekend, but it is only expected to hit the north west of England and Scotland, which have been the wettest parts of the country this summer. The north west has only had 9pc of its expected precipitation.

Article continues below

It is not expected to rain this weekend in the driest parts of the UK, fuelling fears of ‘flash drought’, where drought rapidly develops, could spread across the country.

Flash drought happened in 2022, when crops failed and food prices rose subsequently.

News.title: Burnham pulls back on suggestion to increase income tax allowance
News.content:
Andy Burnham has pulled back from suggestions about increasing the tax-free personal allowance.

The Â£12,570 threshold has been frozen since 2021, resulting in more people being dragged into paying tax as earnings increase.

Burnham told the Times over the weekend that the "frustration about the personal allowance" he had heard while campaigning in the Makerfield by-election was "lodged in my mind".

The prime minister then told reporters on Monday that "all of this will be looked at" in the next budget but conceded any change would be expensive and "difficult given the financial circumstances in which we find ourselves".

Those close to Burnham have since told BBC News that any changes to the personal allowance are not part of his initial plan to tackle the cost of living.

It comes after Burnham told his first cabinet meeting: "We've got to show fiscal discipline. We've got to show that our commitment to the fiscal rules is real and we're prepared to make difficult decisions in relation to that."

Burnham has committed to Labour's 2024 manifesto, which included a promise not to increase the basic, higher, or additional rates of income tax.

That would rule out increasing the top rate of income tax paid by higher earners to offset the cost of lifting the personal allowance.

The Institute for Fiscal Studies has estimated that unfreezing the threshold could end up costing Â£8.5-9bn a year.

Burnham said on Monday that he was "just kind of showing I have visibility of the issue and the impact it's had."

He told reporters it would be "looked at" in the Budget, but added: "Obviously it's difficult, given the financial circumstances in which we find ourselves."

News.title: More women in their 20s are getting type 2 diabetes, experts warn
News.content:
England is seeing a "worrying increase" in young women in their 20s developing type 2 diabetes, experts at Imperial College London have warned.

The rise has largely occurred since the Covid pandemic and is closely linked to increasing obesity levels, according to an analysis of NHS data from 2011 to 2024, external.

Type 2 diabetes is serious, and can lead to severe complications, such as heart attacks and strokes.

When it develops at a younger age, the disease tends to be more aggressive, raising the risk of devastating complications and cutting lives short, according to Diabetes UK.

News.title: 'I can't afford to turn the oven on': 7.4m households struggling to buy essentials
News.content:
Elaine Yates, 77, says money worries mean she "can't remember" the last time she used her oven to cook a hot meal.

"I don't look after myself. I can't remember the last time I put the oven on. I have got an air fryer that I probably used about three weeks ago.

"I had two slices of toast yesterday and two Weetabix and fruit is all I've had to eat today."

The pensioner lives by herself in rural Northamptonshire after being widowed five years ago. Following 20 years as a full-time carer for her husband, her finances are "extremely tight", so she has felt particularly vulnerable to price rises since he passed away.

"It's really hard times, not just for me, but for thousands of others. My car costs me an arm and a leg. The fuel prices are rocketing up again, and I live in a village, so I need a car because I've got arthritis and I can't walk very far. I spend about Â£50 a week on petrol, which is more than my food bill."

Elaine often gives lifts to others in her village who don't have transport, only to find herself unable to shop alongside them.

"I've got one friend who buys clothes and I sit outside the shop because I can't afford to go in," she says. "I can't remember the last time I treated myself."

In the winter, Elaine rarely turns the heating on, and when she does she keeps the thermostat at a low 13C.

News.title: UK humanitarian worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital
News.content:
A humanitarian worker in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been medically evacuated to the UK after a potential healthcareârelated exposure to Ebola.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said the individual, who is a UK resident and has not been named, has no symptoms, and the move is purely precautionary.

The individual remains well but is being assessed and monitored at a London hospital, the statement from UKHSA said.

The hospital has not been named but the Royal Free in north London has a high level isolation unit and is the primary national centre for high consequence infectious diseases.

The incubation period of Ebola ranges from two to 21 days and the humanitarian worker will be required to isolate throughout.

The individual had been working with a humanitarian organisation supporting the Ebola outbreak response.

Ebola is a highly dangerous pathogen. Unlike flu or Covid, it is not airborne and spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids.

Symptoms come on suddenly and start like the flu or malaria, with fever, headache and tiredness. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

Richard Pebody, director of epidemic and emerging infections at UKHSA, said: "The risk to the general public remains low.

"This individual has been transferred out of an abundance of caution, and we're pleased they remain well."

There are currently no confirmed cases of Ebola in the UK, the agency said.

News.title: Judge rules Trump must hand over records sought by BBC in defamation case
News.content:
A judge in Florida has ruled President Donald Trump must hand over financial records sought by the BBC as it defends itself in his $10bn (Â£7.5bn) defamation lawsuit.

The order came during the first hearing in the case, in which the US president is suing the corporation over an episode of Panorama that edited together different sections of his speech on the day of the US Capitol riot on 6 January 2021.

Judge EnjoliquÃ© Lett granted a motion by the BBC's legal team to compel the release of financial records held by the Donald J Trump Revocable Trust, which he created to manage his businesses while he is president.

The judge's ruling at Tuesday's hearing in Miami can still be appealed.

However, it amounts to a partial success in the BBC's attempt to force Trump to provide evidence for his claim of financial loss due to the Panorama edit.

The judge gave a split decision on a separate request by the BBC for documents relating to the Capitol riot itself.

News.title: Great Apes kiss and cuddle to keep the peace, says study
News.content:
Touching, embracing and kissing before stressful events may be an ancient way of building trust, according to scientists studying the behaviour of our closest ape relatives.

Researchers at Durham University studied chimpanzees and bonobos using physical contact to reassure each other ahead of conflicts over food.

One of the most surprising findings was that chimpanzees, despite their reputation for aggression, engaged in close contact, including placing fingers in one another's mouths.

"Before stressful events, they come together, they reassure each other, they touch each other, they hug each other," said Prof Zanna Clay.

News.title: Chris Mason: Another Starmer critic gets promotion as Sarwar joins Burnham government
News.content:
The imminent appointment of the Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar to Andy Burnham's government, via a seat in the House of Lords, sees the promotion of another key figure in the downfall of Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister.

When Sarwar said publicly, back in February, that Sir Keir should stand down, it was a moment of colossal jeopardy for the now former prime minister.

It looked, briefly, like it might bring about an immediate and irrevocable collapse in his authority. Then, one after another, cabinet ministers posted their support for him on social media.

As I wrote at the time, missives of public loyalty from cabinet ministers towards a prime minister shouldn't be newsworthy and they only become so when the opposite seems feasible.

Now, five months on, Sarwar will be swapping Holyrood for Westminster and becoming a minister.

He will be joining Miatta Fahnbulleh in government, the new energy secretary in Burnham's cabinet, who was the first government minister to resign from Sir Keir's administration saying she had lost faith in him.

Also around the cabinet table, the new Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who let it be known in what turned out to be Sir Keir's final weeks in office that he had suggested to him that he ought to accept that his time was up.

It is also worth mentioning too John Healey, who resigned as defence secretary, and Wes Streeting, who resigned as health secretary towards the end of Sir Keir's time in Downing Street, are now in prominent roles in Burnham's cabinet as chancellor and defence secretary respectively.

This is the backdrop to comments from Steve Reed, the former communities secretary and doughty defender of Sir Keir at some of his moments of most intense peril.

Reed wrote to Burnham as he left government and said: "I hope those who did not show loyalty to Keir will now show it to you. I am proud that I acted with integrity at every step over the turbulent past few months."

There is, right now, as you would expect, overwhelming support for Burnham among Labour MPs.

But these public remarks from Reed are an indicator of the wells of private hurt and anger created by the events of recent days, weeks and months.

It is a reminder that, of course, all the folk you are reading and hearing about are human beings who have each keenly felt the tremors of uncertainty in recent months â and depending on their circumstances, outlook, instincts and judgement, have arrived at differing conclusions and decisions about how to act.

The public intervention of Darren Jones, another loyal lieutenant of the former prime minister, taking a swipe at the funding of the government's planned cut in VAT on domestic electricity bills should be seen in this context too.

Labour's switch from one leader to another was less drawn out and dramatic than it might have been, as there was neither a formal leadership challenge to Sir Keir, nor more than one contender to replace him once he had announced his intention to go.

But it is also true that what we have witnessed the climax of this week, and the build up to for months on end, is not cost or pain free for a political party and some of that is manifesting itself now â and may still do for some time.

News.title: Will AI help you do your job or replace you?
News.content:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) companies are making vast claims about the ability of their tools to replace human labour.

Some jobs will be automated, others will be "augmented". The bosses of the world's biggest companies are diverting vast sums into these tools, partly with the knowledge that they could save money on headcount.

"Flat is the new up", we are told, in terms of the size of a company's workforce as investors ask whether jobs should be done by new recruits - or, instead, armies of "AI Agents", virtual workers tasked with doing specific roles, some of them relatively skilled.

If even half true there will be an impact on us all, across sectors and individual careers, and perhaps it will happen sooner than we think.

Nobel prize-winning economists recently warned the world âmust act nowâ, external to ensure that AI leads to rising living standards and not large-scale job displacement, and last month London businesses warned they were struggling to find the skills they need as AI disrupts the jobs market.

It is early days yet, but there are already some notable patterns in the data.

News.title: Burnham tells cabinet to tackle living costs at first meeting
News.content:
Andy Burnham has promised to lead a "cost of living government," as he chaired his first cabinet meeting as prime minister.

He told his newly assembled top team that he wanted to make living expenses a key priority, and give people a "sense that help is coming" on costs.

It comes after he announced a VAT cut to household energy bills from October, in his first major announcement since taking office.

But his plan to pay for the policy by scrapping Sir Keir Starmer's digital ID scheme led to an early row over whether the plan was properly funded.

Downing Street said the estimated Â£850m cost of the VAT cut over the rest of the financial year could come from Â£1.8bn earmarked by the previous government to roll out the digital ID scheme in the next three years.

But Darren Jones, who was among a clutch of Starmer loyalists sacked from the cabinet on Monday, said the ID programme was "unfunded" and Burnham would need to set out where the money would be found.

Opposition parties also seized on the announcement, pointing out the government's budget watchdog has previously said the money to fund digital ID was due to be found from within existing budgets.

"We are only one day in and already Labour are playing fast and loose with the public finances," said Conservative shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride.

The PM's spokesman insisted the policy would be funded by redirecting "savings" identified by departments to cover the cost of the ID scheme.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe was hit on head 21 times with hammer, prosecutors say
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe was hit on the head with a hammer 21 times at her home as she ate lunch in an attack that was caught on camera, prosecutors have told Westminster Magistrates' Court.

Prosecutor Kashif Malik said the man charged with her murder, Joshua Kerry, arrived at her house on 8 July in a red Vauxhall Corsa and entered through the front door.

Kerry, who prosecutors say was in the property for two minutes and was wearing black gloves, then allegedly hit Widdecombe repeatedly with a hammer in her kitchen, tipped her from her chair and took her wallet before driving off.

The 28-year-old from South Yorkshire later also appeared at the Old Bailey and was remanded in custody.

At the Old Bailey hearing, prosecutor Alistair Richardson said the attack on Widdecombe had been carried out with a "ferocity of violence".

Malik told the court that Widdecombe did not attend a pre-arranged online interview with Channel 5's Matt Allwright show that had been scheduled for just before 13:00 BST on 8 July.

The show's production team tried to contact Widdecombe through her personal assistant, who then asked Widdecombe's gardener to check on her, the court heard.

Prosecutors said the gardener entered the house via the open front door on 9 July and found Widdecombe lying face down on her kitchen floor with a serious head injury.

News.title: Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar set to become a minister in Burnham's government
News.content:
Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar is set to stand down to become a minister in Andy Burnham's government.

It would mean Sarwar leaving the Scottish Parliament and his leader role, then taking up a seat in the House of Lords.

Sarwar publicly called for Sir Keir Starmer to resign in February, provoking a political near-death experience for the then prime minister.

It is thought Sarwar, who has led the Scottish Labour Party since 2021, will become a business minister.

He was at the event in London last Friday when Burnham became the new Labour Party leader.

Scottish Labour won just 17 seats out of 129 in the Scottish Parliament elections in May.

News.title: Parts of the UK move closer to drought
News.content:
Summer so far has been exceptionally hot and dry across much of the UK, with three widespread heatwaves and the longest run of dry days in central England since 1995. England, Wales and eastern Scotland have been the driest areas over recent weeks, and this follows a very dry spring in similar regions.

England has received only 3% of its long-term average July rainfall with the south and east of England seeing no rain at all. Wisley in Surrey has seen 33 consecutive dry days.

Rainfall so far this summer has been below average across the UK as a whole, but there has been large regional contrast.

Up to the middle of summer - 15 July - parts of eastern and north-eastern England had received just 26% of their total expected summer rainfall. Areas of northern and western Scotland had more than average for the first half of the summer, though.

In Wales, where just 5% of July rainfall has fallen, Natural Resources Wales has moved the worst affected regions in the north and south-east into "prolonged dry weather status", the first step in its drought plan.

Comparisons are being made with last summer, when drought was declared across much of England, Wales and eastern Scotland. It officially ended just four months ago.

This year, drought has not developed as quickly because heavy rainfall recharged our aquifers, rivers and reservoirs during a very wet autumn and winter.

However, the UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology says flash droughts, external with a sudden transition between wet and dry conditions are "likely to happen more often, and be more intense".

As the effects of human-induced climate change continue, the Met Office expects our summers to become hotter and drier, external in the future. In fact, by 2070, our summers could be up to 60% drier and 1-6C warmer compared to 1990.

News.title: Thames Water announces hosepipe ban for 10 million
News.content:
Thames Water has announced a hosepipe ban affecting 10.1 million customers after an "exceptionally warm and dry spring".

The restrictions mean, from Thursday, hosepipes should not be used for watering gardens or allotments, cleaning cars, filling paddling pools or swimming pools, or cleaning windows.

The water company said its region had seen 40% of average rainfall, and more days at or above 34C this year than ever recorded before.

Nevil Muncaster, director of strategic water resources, said: "We would not be taking this step unless it was necessary to protect water supplies for everyone and the environment."

The ban applies to all customers that Thames Water supplies with drinking water and comes into effect on Thursday.

The company provides water to customers across parts of Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, Surrey, the Thames Valley, Greater London, and the surrounding areas, external.

It provides water and wastewater services to 16 million customers overall.

It said water use was currently 10% above normal in the Thames Valley and Home Counties and 7% above normal in London, which amounted to an extra 100 million litres of water every day.

News.title: Russian warship carried out firing exercise off Plymouth coast
News.content:
The live-fire exercise took place in international waters and lasted for 30 minutes.

The Russian warship requested that the Royal Navy's HMS Tyne reposition to a safer distance, which it did.

The Russian frigate was also being monitored by a French military aircraft which made radio contact with the warship asking it to clarify its intentions, the BBC has been told.

BBC Verify has analysed flight and ship-tracking data which shows the position of HMS Tyne and several British military aircraft operating in and around the Channel near Plymouth on Monday.

Flight data on ADS-B Exchange indicates at least four Royal Air Force and Royal Navy aircraft were flying off the coast of Dorset mostly above the UK's territorial waters, including two Eurofighter Typhoons, a Voyager air refuelling tanker and a Super Lynx helicopter.

A French military H160M GuÃ©pard helicopter also flew out and over the Channel during the afternoon. It is not clear if this is the aircraft which made contact with the Russian warship.

Data on ship-tracking service MarineTraffic shows HMS Tyne began to broadcast its location about 40 miles off Plymouth at 13:57 BST on Monday. It remained in that location for around two hours before departing at 15:56 to return to Plymouth.

HMS Tyne has been tracking Neustrashimy since at least 16 July when both vessels were also captured in the North Sea about 36 miles miles from the port of Felixstowe in Suffolk on a satellite image.

The incident will be a reminder for the new prime minister of increased Russian naval activity near UK waters in recent months.

Last month, Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in a six-hour operation which was the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

Also in June, a British couple in international waters in the English Channel came across a Russian warship - Admiral Grigorovich - 23 miles off the Isle of Wight.

The frigate fired warning shots as Jane and Alan Kelvey sailed their yacht on what Russia's defence ministry said had been a "dangerous approach". However, the couple said they had not been on a "collision course".

Russian warships regularly pass through international waters in the Channel, which are separate from UK and French territorial waters.

News.title: Union plans rail strikes over train safety concerns
News.content:
A union that represents railway staff has announced plans for its members at East Midlands Railway (EMR) to take strike action over "growing safety concerns the company has failed to address".

The RMT union said it had been in dispute with EMR since April following the rollout of the 810 fleet (Aurora), which it said had been operating with a "significant number" of faults.

It said its members planned to take strike action on Saturday 1 August and the following two Saturdays.

An EMR spokesperson said any suggestion that the Hitachi Rail Class 810 fleet did not meet the required safety standards was "incorrect", and added it continued "to engage in discussions with RMT regarding this dispute".

Last week, EMR said reliability and maintenance issues with the new Aurora (Class 810) trains - made by Hitachi Rail - were to blame.

EMR has also outlined "challenges" with both the 810s and the older Class 222s, affecting the toilets, air conditioning and catering equipment.

It added the Class 222 trains had also required "additional maintenance support to accommodate increased running and operational requirements".

The operator first introduced the Aurora trains into passenger service in December, after what EMR said was a three-year delay.

News.title: Family of woman who lay dead in crash for days confronts mechanic who falsified MOT
News.content:
Angry scenes erupted outside court after the family of a woman killed in a car crash confronted a garage owner who falsified an MOT just weeks before.

Neil John Lewis, 47, pleaded guilty to fraud by false representation at Cardiff Magistrates' Court on Tuesday, and admitted he knew the car was "dangerous".

Eve Smith, 21, Darcy Ross, 21, and Rafel Jeanne, 24, died when the car given the false MOT crashed into woodland in Cardiff in March 2023. They lay undiscovered for two days. Two others survived.

As Lewis left court, the family of Ross brandished a framed photograph the dead woman, and shouted at him: "Darcy Ross, remember her name."
