“All aside whatever happened in previous weeks, that was soon forgotten. I really respected him for that.”

Sports.title: ‘Reclaim football’: Sepp Blatter joins La Liga chief in call for Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has come in for heavy criticism from his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, and the La Liga president, Javier Tebas, with the pair united in the belief that he should stand down.

As Spain celebrated their World Cup win on Sunday, Tebas accused Infantino of “destroying the football industry” by prioritising the World Cup over national competitions. He claimed “his time is up”. Blatter has called for “fans, players and national associations to reclaim football and bring it back to its roots under new leadership”.

Tebas is particularly opposed to the Fifa president’s enthusiasm for expanding the 2030 tournament to 64 teams from 48. “Increasing the number of national teams makes no sense,” Tebas told Italy’s La Gazzetta dello Sport.

“The football industry is not just the World Cup. Not everything can revolve around the World Cup. It is national competitions that support this sport.

“They [Fifa] are destroying the football industry, which generates tens of thousands of jobs, for an event that lasts 40 days and involves a minority of players. We need fewer national teams and more protection for national football, at all levels. They don’t realise they are making irresponsible decisions.”

Tebas believes Infantino should resign, although he admits he finds it hard to envisage such a scenario. “He has the support of the system, of the federations. There is no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. It is a system rotten at its core.”

Scandal-proof: why Infantino’s Fifa power can’t be touched – video

After 10 years at Fifa’s helm, Infantino is poised to be re‑elected for a fourth term in March, potentially standing unopposed for the third time in a row, but Tebas believed the Swiss was a World Cup win away from being forced out. He argues that had the USA defeated Belgium in their last‑16 game Infantino might been mired in an unrecoverable scandal.

The USA striker Folarin Balogun had a one-match ban suspended by the Fifa disciplinary committee, facilitating his involvement against Belgium. The decision was taken after a phone call made to Infantino by Donald Trump. Infantino said the decision to overturn Balogun’s ban was made independently by its disciplinary committee “based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts”.

Tebas said: “The suspension of the American player’s ban was absolutely serious. They were lucky Belgium eliminated the USA because a case could have arisen that might have cost Infantino his job. Since Belgium won they were able to bury the matter. But these things are just the tip of the iceberg.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Blatter, a controversial figure during his tenure as Fifa president, appears to regard the Balogun case as a tipping point. “The longest World Cup has come to an end with the right champions,” he wrote on X. “But on the way to the final whistle, the tournament lost its credibility. Politics must not be allowed to overshadow the game.”

Tebas feels much the same about hydration breaks and extended half‑time intervals. “Fifa arranges things as it wants, for what it wants, for its own interests, certainly not football,” he said. “So if they need a 27-minute half-time break, they’ll have it.

“Hydration breaks are a lie. We have them in La Liga, but when it’s genuinely hot. The pitches in Dallas, Los Angeles, Atlanta had air conditioning; I had to put a jumper on in the stands. It was a lie, a break for advertising.”

Fifa has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Dark truth of $1.5BILLION 'gas station heroin' secretly rife in sports after cops found it on tragic NBA star, 29, weeks before death
Sports.content:
On April 1, NBA star Brandon Clarke was arrested for overtaking multiple vehicles at more than 100mph in a no-passing zone in eastern Arkansas.

But the officers searching his Corvette had their attention attracted elsewhere. They found a blue duffle bag with multiple small packages containing green powder.

'It's just kratom, it is legal,' Clarke insisted. Kratom is legal in most states but was banned in Arkansas, where he had encountered police.

Six weeks later, Clarke was dead.

'Kratom is an addictive substance. It can, and does, kill,' Dr Josef G Thundiyil, a medical toxicologist and emergency physician with Orlando Health, told the Daily Mail.

Kratom is sold legally in smoke shops, convenience stores and online. Marketed as a natural wellness product, kratom, which has since been dubbed 'gas station heroin,' has grown into an estimated $1.5billion-a-year industry, according to the American Kratom Association.

Memphis Grizzlies star Brandon Clarke died at the age of 29 in May of this year

Police in Arkansas found kratom, otherwise known as 'gas station heroin,' on Clarke during his arrest weeks before his death

In the same botanical family as coffee, kratom is derived from the leaves of a tropical tree native to Southeast Asia and has been used there for centuries. Only recently has it gained in popularity in the US for purported pain relief and stamina benefits.

Sold in brightly-colored cans resembling energy drinks, capsules pass as everyday vitamins or sugar-coated gummies. But experts say looks are deceiving.

'That it's sold very unregulated in tea shops, smoke shops, gives a false reassurance,' Dr Thundiyil explained.

He warned, a 'whole host' of negative and dangerous side effects have been reported amid kratom's boom, including 'severe compulsive addiction.'

'Users describe: I feel it's just as bad as when I was on an opioid, meaning it's very addictive,' he continued. 'And what we have found of the different outcomes, we've seen reported things like seizures and liver failure. But the one that really caught our attention was death.'

A government report showed poison center calls about kratom have skyrocketed. In 2025 alone, they jumped 1,200 percent to 3,400. There were 233 kratom-associated deaths reported between 2015 and 2025, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Many incidents are a consequence of kratom being mixed with alcohol or other drugs.

'[Kratom] has two different ways of working,' Dr Zaid Fadul, a board-certified physician and founder of Bespoke Concierge MD, told Daily Mail. 'At low doses, it can be a stimulant and can cause pain relief.

In the same botanical family as coffee, kratom comes from leaves of a tree native to Asia

Kratom comes in brightly-colored cans resembling energy drinks and capsules look like candy

'Higher doses have different effects. It can be sedating. Any dose for a prolonged period of time, you get chemical dependence, then eventually addiction.'

The risks don't end there. Dehydration is a side effect, triggered by the loss of appetite caused by kratom, Dr Fadul said.

'Two, kratom is going to mask pain,' he added. 'It's not going to treat pain.'

Kratom does not treat injuries. Instead, it lessens pain for athletes to continue training and competing.

'That's when a stress fracture turns into a real fracture,' Dr Fadul said. 'You want recovery for athletes. You don't want pain masking. You want real recovery.'

In an industry where the body is the money-maker, preserving health is key - and kratom puts that in jeopardy.

Given its accessibility and legal status, it is a product athletes may not necessarily have to disclose to teams and risk a trade.

'I get that athletes are hesitant to take opioids, or they want to get off opioids, and so they're looking for alternatives,' Dr Thundiyil said. 'My warning would be kratom is probably not that solution; it's unproven.

Clarke died near Los Angeles, where he had been staying with a friend from college

An investigation into the power forward's death is still ongoing

'The harms are growing. You may be jumping out the pot and into the fire.'

Clarke was discovered with 235 grams of kratom in April.

The Canadian-American star was restricted to two games for the Grizzlies' last season with injury. He missed 73 games, sitting out 26 recovering from surgery on his right knee before another 46 with a right calf strain.

In addition to kratom, Clarke had a THC vape pen and a prescription for a common painkiller used to treat sporting injuries when he was arrested

'That right there is legal pain medicine,' Clarke said in the dashcam video of his arrest. 'That's Toradol.'

Six weeks later, Clarke was found dead on May 12 in the San Fernando Valley. His death is being investigated as a potential overdose after drug paraphernalia was found at the scene.

No official cause has been announced and the inquest is ongoing.

Clarke and a woman attend his sister's 2024 wedding in Mexico City, Mexico

Clarke poses for a picture with his mother, Whitney Triplett, his step father and his half siblings

Clarke is not alone.

UFC veteran Diego Sanchez's former coach Joshua Fabia accused him of being 'strung out' on kratom and other substances in 2021. Fabia claimed the fighter was an 'addict' following their split. Sanchez denied the allegations.

Wrestler Sabu was allegedly given kratom ahead of his final match amid fears he would not show up to the ring, fellow wrestler Joey Janela claimed in a 2025 interview. Janela later claimed that Sabu - whose real name was Terrance Brunk - took kratom 'daily for years' to help him get off other substances.

Sabu died at age 61 in May 2025 three weeks after his final match. GCW, which hosted the bout, denied any involvement in his death.

Meanwhile, the United Football League - the eight-team spring football league - embraced CBD Kratom in 2024 as its official partner, highlighting potential to 'enhance physical performance’ as well as ‘kratom's ability to aid in chronic pain’.

The Missouri Attorney General's Office launched an investigation into CBD Kratom in November for 'deception, fraud, false promises' among other acts. It is one of nearly two dozen kratom companies under investigation by the Missouri AG office. The UFL's partnership ended before the start of this season.

CBD Kratom, meanwhile, said it relished an 'opportunity to demonstrate the strength of our safety standards, compliance practices, and long-standing commitment to consumer education.'

UFC veteran Diego Sanchez (right) denied accusations of being 'strung out' on kratom

Kratom is not considered performance-enhancing by the World Anti-Doping Agency. It was briefly monitored by WADA but removed from the tracking list in 2018.

The United States Anti-Doping Agency, which handles the drug testing for Olympians, explicitly advises against using it over health hazards, but has not banned it.

In Tennessee, where Clarke played for the Grizzlies, kratom was legal when he was arrested. Three months later, Tennessee became the latest state to ban it, with the illegal status enforced from July 1.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's full humiliation laid bare: Left crying as his Argentine thugs disgraced themselves... how this World Cup exposed the GOAT's dark arts shame
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's full humiliation laid bare: Left crying as his Argentine thugs disgraced themselves... how this World Cup exposed the GOAT's dark arts shame

Like so many sporting greats, Lionel Messi did not get the fairytale ending that his illustrious career deserved in New Jersey on Sunday night.

Throughout history it has proven a rarity for legendary athletes to exit the big stage on a high. Muhammad Ali lost three of his final four fights before hanging up his gloves. Michael Jordan bowed out from the NBA after failing to make the playoffs for a second straight year with the Washington Wizards. Tom Brady waved goodbye to football after a postseason loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Babe Ruth, Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal... the list runs long. And now Messi's name has been added to it. Well, at least when it comes to the World Cup.

The sad sight of Argentina's icon shedding tears after their final defeat to Spain says it all. At 39, it is almost certain this was his closing chapter on soccer's grandest stage. He will be 43 when the next one rolls around.

Yet Messi didn't just sign off from the World Cup on the back of a loss. It was as miserable and shameful of a night as it could be for his country at MetLife Stadium.

After becoming the first finalists in history to fail to register a single shot in 90 minutes - and not testing Spain's goalkeeper Unai Simon once in 120 - Argentina's sore losers resorted to thuggery when Spain celebrated their triumph at full-time.

Lionel Messi did not get his fairytale ending as Argentina lost to Spain in the World Cup final

The Argentina icon exited the biggest stage in soccer on the most depressing of notes

Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the biggest villain, grabbing Spain's Eric Garcia by the neck and punching midfielder Gavi in the face before pushing him over. Defender Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso, while even a 53-year-old Argentine assistant coach landed a punch on Spain's Dani Olmo.

While he was not involved in the violence, Messi is captain of this team and what will likely prove his World Cup finale will always be remembered for the ugly scenes at full time.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner didn't cover himself in glory, either. In the wake of a red card for Argentina's Enzo Fernandez, Messi embarrassed himself with an attempt to send Marc Cucurella down the tunnel.

After Cucurella spoke to him while briefly covering his mouth, Messi stuck his arm in the air and signaled to the referee to try and get the Spain man sent off. FIFA's new rules forbid players from concealing conversations.

Fortunately, the official did not bow to the pressure of one of the game's finest ever players. But the sight of an all-time great, renowned for modesty on and off the field, resorting to dirty tactics was grim.

'One of the most pathetic things I've ever seen from a supposed sportsman,' Piers Morgan fumed on X about the incident. 'Messi's fake halo shattered in this World Cup; he was the sneaky cheating leader of a vile bunch of violent thugs.'

Once they'd grown tired of lashing out, the now-former world champions made it a masterclass in bitterness by refusing to form a guard of honor for Spain and turning their backs as their competitors lifted the World Cup.

They then sparked ugly scenes at full time by lashing out at Spain as they celebrated the win

Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the neck and punching Gavi before pushing him over

Messi also embarrassed himself with his desperate attempt to get Marc Cucurella sent off

Cucurella briefly touched his mouth while talking to Messi - players are sent off for covering their face while talking to opponents

The closing shot of Messi at a World Cup will forever be crying with his back to the trophy lift, surrounded by his henchmen, in a moment more befitting of 10-year-old children than elite athletes.

If that wasn't bad enough, Argentina skipped mandatory post-game media interviews and fled the stadium.

Messi is known for humility while cementing his status as arguably the greatest of all time, with the petulant antics of famous rival Cristiano Ronaldo - often accused of hogging the limelight and not being a good teammate - painting him in a better light.

Nevertheless, soccer's golden boy bid farewell to the World Cup with most wanting him to lose. He did exactly that, without managing a shot on target before Argentina disgraced themselves.

Other than fan footage of her leaving the stadium under the protection of burly security guards, there were also mysteriously few sightings of Messi's stunning wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, at Sunday's final.

It was a far cry from her usually-frequent appearances at the front of the stadium's VIP suites, cheering her man on alongside their children. How poignant, then, for her to be in hiding as Messi struggled and wept on a devastating day.

There were few sightings of Messi's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, at the final other than her leaving

It took Antonela a day before she paid tribute to her husband on social media after the loss

She broke her silence a day later, writing on Instagram: 'You will always be the best. Thank you for showing us every day that true success is built through hard work, sacrifice, and perseverance - without ever losing sight of who you really are.

'You are the best example for our children and an inspiration to millions of people. I admire you more than words can express, and I feel immensely proud to walk through life by your side.'

All in all, it was an anticlimactic end for the Messi family at his sport's most prestigious competition.

Even his all-time World Cup goals record no longer remains. Less than a month after leapfrogging Germany icon Miroslav Klose in Argentina's second group-stage outing against Austria, France superstar Kylian Mbappe's brace in the third-place playoff took him one ahead of Messi on 21.

So what next? Messi has half the season to finish with Inter Miami, who return to action Wednesday after MLS's World Cup break.

But Messi won't play in their first game back against Chicago Fire, nor their trip to CF Montreal on Saturday.

According to ESPN, he'll also skip the MLS All-Star Game on July 29, too. It would be the third time Messi has been selected for the annual showpiece. He is yet to play in a single one.

A more likely return is Miami's clash with Columbus Crew on Saturday August 1.

Once back up and running at club level, Messi has over two years remaining on his current deal with the team, which extends beyond the 2028 Copa America.

Messi may stick around at club level for a while but he will surely retire from Argentina duty

When he's still operating at such a high level - he still scored eight World Cup goals this year - it would be a shock to see him end that contract early.

As for his international career, it remains to be seen whether Messi calls it a day after two consecutive World Cup final appearances. It would make most sense.

Prior to the final he hinted as such by referring to it as 'The Last Tango' in a post on social media. Following the defeat, he also shared an emotional message on Instagram which felt like a farewell.

'The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal,' he wrote. 'But I also hold onto all the good things.

'Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.'

Presumably through gritted teeth, he added: 'I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship.'

If only he and Argentina could have done a better job of that on the field.

Sports.title: New boss Vrancken laments Hearts' failings after nightmare first match in charge
Sports.content:
Wouter Vrancken bemoaned his players’ lack of efficiency in both boxes as Hearts slumped to a nightmare 4-0 defeat in the first leg of their Champions League second qualifying round tie in Austria.

It was a horrendous first match in charge for Belgian coach Vrancken who replaced Derek McInnes in the Hearts hot seat this summer.

Despite dominating possession and having more touches in the opposition box than Sturm Graz, Vrancken’s side suffered a crushing loss which effectively ends their hopes of further progress in Europe’s elite club competition.

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken despairs as his new charges suffer in Austria

Hearts were guilty of shocking defending, especially at set pieces, as goals from Jon Stankovic, Jeyland Mitchell, Luca Weindhandl and Jurgen Heil put Graz in total control.

The visitors also missed several clear-cut chances of their own with Pierre Landry-Kabore and Alexander Kyziridis especially culpable when the score was still 1-0.

‘We didn’t start too badly but then conceded from a set piece,’ said Vrancken. ‘That was the summary of the game, we got killed by two set pieces at the start of the first half and second half.

‘After the first goal, we needed some minutes to come back into it and find our confidence again. We did pretty well and created a lot of chances which we needed to do much better with.

‘They were 100 per cent chances and at this level, you have to score them. I was pretty confident at half-time that we could still turn it around.

‘Then the second half started and after we missed the first good opportunity again, we conceded from another set piece.

Graz celebrate after Stankovic scores the early opening goal for Graz

‘Then it is difficult in their heads for the players. Sometimes you try to force it and make it more difficult for yourself. When you don’t kill (teams) yourself, you get killed. It’s a pity.

‘We had to be more efficient and Sturm Graz were more efficient than us tonight. It’s no excuse. We showed in the game that we had a lot of possession and created a lot of chances from it.’

Hearts now look set to drop into the Europa League, where they would face either Benfica or St Gallen in the third qualifying round, but Vrancken insists he hasn’t given up hope of overseeing a dramatic comeback in the return leg against Sturm Graz at Tynecastle next Tuesday.

‘You have to believe it,’ he said. ‘Especially at Tynecastle with the support of our fans. The ones who were here tonight were amazing, even with this result.

‘So we have go full out next week. If we are more efficient in the first half, then you never know. We could score some goals and there could be magic there. In this scenario, we still have to believe it.'

Sports.title: Sturm Graz 4-0 Hearts: Wouter Vrancken's bold vision falls apart on a night of disorganised disaster with Jam Tarts' Champions League hopes in tatters
Sports.content:
Sturm Graz 4-0 Hearts: Wouter Vrancken's bold vision falls apart on a night of disorganised disaster with Jam Tarts' Champions League hopes in tatters

Wouter Vrancken describes the style of play he likes to instil in his teams as ‘organised chaos’.

On a truly calamitous night in southern Austria, it was quite simply a disorganised disaster as the Belgian coach saw his Hearts tenure get off to the worst possible start.

It was all risk and no reward for the Gorgie club as Sturm Graz took an iron grip on this Champions League second qualifying round tie.

Defensively, Hearts were an absolute mess as Graz captain Jon Stankovic’s fourth minute opener was followed by a flurry of three goals in a torrid nine-minute spell early in the second half.

Barring a remarkable turnaround at Tynecastle next Tuesday night, Hearts will be dropping down into the Europa League qualifiers where it won’t get much easier for Vrancken.

The 47-year-old clearly needs time to bed his ideas in but will quickly find himself under serious pressure unless he restores some of the defensive discipline which was the hallmark of Hearts’ effectiveness under Derek McInnes last season.

Vrancken is left with questions to answer following a 4-0 hammering in Austria

It had been just 68 days since they lost out on the Premiership title in such agonising circumstances at Celtic Park and amid the pain experienced by club and supporters that afternoon, it was easy to lose sight of the fact they had still secured Champions League participation for the first time in 20 years.

Despite all of the close season upheaval at Tynecastle, with the departures of manager McInnes and key playing duo Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin to Rangers, new boss Vrancken relied on as many established squad members as possible for his opening night in the job.

Only two of Hearts new signings - defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott and winger Calvin Miller - were in the starting line-up named by Vrancken.

If he was looking to establish some early stability, however, Vrancken instead suffered disruption with the cheap and early concession of Sturm Graz’s opener.

It was Hearts who seemed to have made the brighter start, Christian Borchgrevink firing a shot over after Graz keeper Daniil Khudiakov unconvincingly palmed out Harry Milne’s low cross in the opening minute.

That sign of encouragement for the travelling fans was wiped out as Hearts completely switched off at the back when Jeyland Mitchell launched a long throw into their penalty area from the left. Jamie McCart was caught on his heels as Stankovic rose to guide a simple close range header beyond Alexander Schwolow.

The expansive and pacy attacking style of play Vrancken is renowned for was certainly evident but while Hearts looked good in possession, they remained wide open at the back.

Stankovic celebrates after Sturm Graz go 1-0 up inside four minutes

Graz missed a glaring opportunity to double their lead in the 10th minute when Simon Seidl’s corner was flicked on by Stankovic before Seedy Jatta hit a post with a free header from inside the six yard box.

When Schwolow had to react smartly to keep out a deflected shot from Jacob Hodl, there was a danger of the tie running away from Hearts.

They carved out plenty of menacing opportunities of their own, however, against a Graz defence which also appeared vulnerable.

After Claudio Braga had a low shot held by Khudiakov, Hearts should have equalised in the 25th minute. Oisin McEntee’s surging run carved a path into the Graz penalty area and the Irish midfielder showed great awareness to pick out Pierre Landry Kabore with his cutback.

It was a bread and butter chance for the big striker but with only Khudiakov to beat, he steered his shot straight into the grateful arms of the Russian keeper.

Graz went straight up the other end and Fagan-Walcott spared the blushes of his central defensive partner McCart who had played Jatta onside. The Norwegian striker looked certain to score until Fagan-Walcott slid in to make a brilliant block.

New arrival Guendouz is left frustrated after failing to make an impact

Neither side were willing to resort to a cautious approach as the contest continued to ebb and flow. Hearts wasted their best chance yet to level matters in the 34th minute. Braga won the ball high up the pitch and slid it to Alexandros Kyziridis who was unmarked inside the box.

It was the definition of a sitter but the Greek winger inexplicably sidefooted his shot wide of Khudiakov’s left hand post.

There was an anxious moment for Hearts six minutes before half-time when Hungarian referee Gergo Bogar pointed to the spot after Milne had slid in to block a shot from Szymon Wlodarczyk. While the ball hit the full-back’s arm, it did so only after bouncing up off his leg and a VAR review correctly saw the decision overturned.

Hearts’ start to the second half was the stuff of nightmares as Graz ran riot. The visitors were undone by another simple set piece when Mitchell had a free back post run to head home half-time sub Otar Kiteishvili’s corner from the left in the 50th minute.

Three minutes later, it was 3-0 when teenager Luca Weinhandl’s deflected shot beat Schwolow after Hearts made a mess of several chances to clear the danger.

They were carved wide open again in the 59th minute as Jurgen Heil played a one-two with Weinhandl on the right of the box before slamming the ball home.

Vrancken made a raft of changes in the closing half hour but Tom Renaud’s shot over was the closest Hearts came to pulling a goal back and perhaps giving them a sliver of hope for the second leg.

As it is, their long-awaited return to the Champions League looks as good as over.

Sports.title: West Ham accept £60m bid from Al-Hilal for Crysencio Summerville... with Premier League clubs now unlikely to compete at that price
Sports.content:
Al-Hilal have agreed a £60million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville.

The offer outstrips the £39m plus add-ons tabled by Roma and the Netherlands international has been offered a long-term contract pending his medical.

Final details are being discussed for the 24-year-old but Premier League and European clubs are unlikely to compete with the Saudi offer.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, Netherlands international Summerville was on Manchester United's radar and they held exploratory talks with West Ham.

Summerville joined the Hammers from Leeds for £25m in the summer of 2024 and scored eight goals in 56 games for the club but was unable to help them avoid relegation to the Championship last season.

West Ham are still looking to offload Jean-Clair Todibo, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Alphonse Areola, Edson Alvarez and Niclas Fullkrug.

Al-Hilal have agreed a £60million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville

With Aston Villa progressing on Alejandro Garnacho talks, Roma are now likely to look at RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa, who also figured lower down on Arsenal's list, and his Norway compatriot Andreas Schjelderup at Benfica. Diego Moreira at Strasbourg has also been floated.

Sports.title: World Cup star Vinicius Jr packs on the PDA with his stunning girlfriend in Rio de Janeiro as he celebrates chin surgery success on lavish vacation
Sports.content:
Fresh off a stunning surgical procedure that altered his face, Brazilian football star Vinicius Junior was seen enjoying time with his girlfriend after an early World Cup exit.

The Real Madrid man was out in the sun at Reserva Beach in Rio de Janeiro with his on-and-off girlfriend Virginia Fonseca.

Cameras captured an intimate moment between the two as Fonseca leaned in and planted a kiss on the footballer.

At one point, Fonseca even noticed the cameras and flashed a smile towards the photographer.

Fonseca and her man continued to enjoy the sun as they relaxed before what should be a lengthy football season.

The photos emerged just hours after it was revealed that Vinicius underwent a stunning procedure.

Real Madrid and Brazil star Vinicius Junior spent time on the beach with his girlfriend

At one point, his partner, Virginia Fonseca, leaned in and planted a kiss on his lips

The pair enjoyed the sunshine after Brazil's early exit from the World Cup

According to Brazilian news outlet TMC, following Brazil's defeat to Norway in the Round of 16, Vinicius headed straight to a dermatologist in Goiania when he landed back in the country following a short vacation in Europe with Fonseca.

A number of photos of the 26-year-old appearing unrecognizable after the op have gone viral on social media, with fans blown away by his remarkable transformation.

Virginia shared a snap of them at her new gym on Monday, having clearly got back together after breaking up before the World Cup, while one of his friends also posted footage of his new-and-improved side profile as he signed a Real Madrid jersey for a fan.

Vinicius posed alongside Dr. Alessandro Alarcao, who performed the surgery in Goiania, in another picture that has emerged online.

He underwent the procedure, which 'uses fillers to sculpt the facial contour', to add more definition to his chin after being cruelly mocked over it during the World Cup.

And it seems like the Madrid player is happy with his dramatic new look, as he is all smiles in all of the post-op photos that have surfaced.

At one point, Fonseca even noticed the cameras and flashed a smile towards the photographer

The pair remained close just hours after photos emerged of Vinicius' new look

The Brazil superstar looks completely different after undergoing chin harmonization surgery

🚨 Vini Jr at the clinic after his chin harmonization surgery. pic.twitter.com/WOq8OC0fgs — Madrid Zone (@theMadridZone) July 20, 2026

Fans were left astonished by the effect of the surgery on social media, with one writing: 'My brain can't wrap itself around the fact that this is Vini Jr. now, I swear'.

Another joked: 'I'll not believe this until I see him coming out to play a match looking like this'.

'MANNNN WHO THE F*** IS THAT,' a third said in bewilderment.

'Oh my God I don’t even recognize him,' a fourth commented.

While another user put: 'Vinicius jr is the first person in history to look like the AI version of himself'.

Vinicius and Brazil endured a frustrating World Cup before being eliminated by Norway at the last-16 stage.

Vinicius jr is the first person in history to look like the AI version of himself 😭😭 pic.twitter.com/Sqhnd3M0bX — Anabella💙❤️ (@AnabellaMarvy) July 21, 2026

Vinicius has added more definition to his chin after being cruelly mocked over it online

He and Brazil were dumped out of the World Cup at the last-16 stage after a 2-1 loss to Norway

After finishing top of Group C, despite looking unconvincing in their opening draw against Morocco, they snatched a dramatic 96th-minute win over Japan in the last 32 after flattering to deceive again.

Carlo Ancelotti's men were then outclassed by Norway in New Jersey, with Erling Haaland's late double putting them out of sight before Neymar scored a consolation from the penalty spot with one of the last kicks of the game.

It wasn't a disastrous tournament for Vinicius from an individual standpoint, nevertheless, after he scored four goals before Brazil's exit.

Once his post-World Cup break is over, he will return to Madrid to begin preseason training ahead of the 2026-27 season.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers completes record move to Chelsea, West Ham agree £60m fee to sell Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal and Ipswich have £10m bid for Daizen Maeda accepted by Celtic: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea complete record Rogers deal

Chelsea have confirmed the signing of Morgan Rogers for a club-record £117m - which also makes him the most expensive British player of all time.

They have also had a £64m move for Alex Scott rejected by Bournemouth, who insist he is not for sale.

For more on this story click HERE

Morgan Rogers seals his £117m move to Chelsea in a deal announced at 9.45pm tonight

Toffees chew over Dewsbury

Everton are taking a look at Bristol Rovers prodigy Ollie Dewsbury.

The 18-year-old has also attracted attention from Arsenal and Fulham but is training with Everton ahead of a possible move.

Dewsbury became the youngest player to represent League Two Rovers in the FA Cup when he made his senior debut against Whitby Town in November 2023. Aged just 15 at the time, it made him the second youngest player to represent the club he has been at since the age of seven.

Palace still in for Matsima

Crystal Palace still working on Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima as a centre back option.

Daily Mail Sport last week reported their interest in the 6ft 4in defender, who has played for France at the Olympics.

Chrislain Matsima battles with Florian Wirtz before the Leverkusen star's move to Liverpool

Welcome (back) to Hull! Zambrano's a Tiger again

Hull City have confirmed the signing of Ecuadorian midfielder Oscar Zambrano from Maribor for an undisclosed fee.

The 22-year-old was on loan at Hull in 2024-25. He has signed a four-year contract, with the club holding an option to extend by a further 12 months.

Fulham set to bid £24m for Saint Shea

Fulham are preparing a £24million offer for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

Leeds United have so far fallen short of Southampton's demands for the Northern Ireland international with the Championship side holding out for £25million plus add-ons.

Leeds have made three proposals with add-ons but with agreement still to be found, Fulham are ready to make their move.

Manager Alvaro Arbeloa is on board with bringing in the 22-year-old who started out at Manchester City and talks are expected to advance.

Charles scored the winning goal against Middlesbrough which looked to have secured their place in the play-off final against Hull City only for Spygate to end their season abruptly.

He was left out of their squad to face Eastleigh in a friendly at the weekend however as he had been afforded more time off after being involved in international friendlies for Northern Ireland.

Shea Charles' goal against Boro looked to have sent Saints to Wembley before they were expelled for the Spygate scandal

Sutton send for City's Spike

Manchester City goalkeeper Spike Brits has joined National League side Sutton United on a season-long loan.

The 19-year-old, an England U18 international, has been at City since 2023 when they brought him in from AFC Wimbledon's academy.

Hull could throw a line for Fisher

Hull are keen on Norwich City right-back Kellen Fisher, 22, but have yet to make a formal bid.

Norwich remain determined to hold onto their first-choice right back this summer despite interest from Premier League sides.

Kellen Fisher competes with Fulham's Willian back in 2023

Forest set to offer £32m for Sporting's Diomande

Nottingham Forest are advancing in their talks for Sporting Lisbon defender Ousmane Diomande.

The centre back was a target for Oliver Glasner at Crystal Palace and the Ivory Coast international is open to moving to the Premier League.

Sources in Portugal say Sporting are pushing for £42million for the centre-back amid interest from AC Milan, Newcastle United, Crystal Palace and Leeds United. Forest are understood to be offering £32m. However, it is understood the other Premier League sides are yet to step up their interest.

Forest are light in central defence with Murillo returning from injury and interest building in Jair Cunha. They have signed Xaver Schlager and are ready to offer over £45m for Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall.

£60m deal agreed for Summerville

Al-Hilal have agreed a £60million deal with West Ham for winger Crysencio Summerville.

The offer outstrips the £39m plus add-ons tabled by Roma and the Netherlands international has been offered a long term contract pending his medical.

Final details are being discussed for the 24-year-old but Premier League and European clubs are unlikely to compete with the Saudi offer.

For more on this story click HERE

Crysencio Summerville has been a target for several clubs this summer

Ipswich's £10m Daizen bid does trick

Ipswich Town have had a £10m bid for Celtic’s Daizen Maeda accepted. A deal worth £8m up front and £2m in add-ons has been agreed in principle.

Earlier this month the forward confirmed his wish to move to England .

‘Since I went to Celtic, I became interested in the Premier League,’ he told Japanese YouTube show Pivot. ‘I started watching a lot of Premier League games. I have a strong desire to play in the Premier League.'

The Tractor Boys have also completed their deal for Leicester winger Abdul Fatawu today, with manager Gary O'Neil saying of the 22-year-old: 'Abdul is a young player who has already gained good experience in the game and we’re excited to have him with us.

'He has strong physical and technical attributes, is comfortable on the ball and can test the opposition in one-on-one situations, so will provide us with good options within the squad.

'Having represented his country at the World Cup this summer, I know he is now looking forward to getting to work ahead of the Premier League season.'

Daizen Maeda played a big role for Japan at the World Cup this summer

Villa likely to seal deal for Garnacho

Aston Villa are expected to land Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho.

After enquiries during conversations over Morgan Rogers’ £117m sale, Villa have proposed a loan for the Argentine with obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

Chelsea have been holding out for a permanent sale around £40m as Manchester United are also due a sell in percentage.

Aston Villa have stepped up their interest in Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho

Roma have also offered a loan with options for Garnacho who was of interest to Villa before he left Manchester United last summer.

Villa remain keen to sign Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea and are monitoring developments with Crysencio Summerville at West Ham.

The Hammers have a £39m offer plus add ons on the table from Roma and have added interest from Al Hilal.

PFA free agent squad in action tonight

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jonny Williams and Egypt international Samy Morsy are in the PFA free agent squad of 21 to face Hednesford Town at Key's Park Stadium at 7.45 pm tonight.

Around 48 players have now joined the PFA pre-season camp where they train and play a series of friendlies to showcase their availability to clubs over the summer.

Former Manchester United and Port Vale keeper Ben Amos and ex-Ipswich Town striker Connor Wickham are among a growing band of players looking to earn contracts elsewhere.

Another friendly is planned at Tranmere Rovers on Friday.

The games can be viewed on the PFA's live YouTube stream.

Spurs agree to sell Lankshear to Middlesbrough

Tottenham have agreed to sell Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough for £14million potentially rising to £20m with add-ons.

There is also a 20 per cent sell on clause and Spurs have matching rights on any bids from other clubs in the future.

Striker Lankshear, 21, who was on loan at Oxford United last season, is expected for a medical later today.

Nicolas Jackson interested in Aston Villa move

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa to work with his former head coach Unai Emery again.

Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson is interested in his potential switch to Aston Villa

Jackson's name came up during conversations between Chelsea and Villa centred on Morgan Rogers, who is set to move to Stamford Bridge for a club-record £117million and sign a six-year deal with the option of an extra year.

Villa have long been admirers of Jackson under Emery, who had the striker at Villarreal. Chelsea have been taking their time to decide on the 25-year-old Senegal international's future.

With Jackson, Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Marc Guiu and Joao Pedro as Xabi Alonso's striker options currently, there is an acceptance inside of Chelsea that they need to reduce their numbers, especially while facing a season out of Europe.

Joao Pedro is considered untouchable and so not for sale. Delap is keen to have another season to prove himself after a disappointing campaign following his move from Ipswich, while Emegha has only just arrived this summer from their sister side Strasbourg. Guiu is expected to leave either permanently or on loan.

There remains a market for Jackson, who spent the last season on loan at Bayern Munich. Chelsea are believed to value him at £65m.

That is down on the £80m they were understood to be seeking last summer before sanctioning his temporary switch to Bayern. That came at a time when the relationship between Jackson and then-manager Enzo Maresca had broken down.

Chelsea's plan for Jackson was to have him return in pre-season so that Xabi Alonso could take a closer look at the scorer. Alonso said at his unveiling last week that Jackson was due to join them on their tour of Australia and Asia after his post-World Cup break.

However, sources close to Jackson have told Daily Mail Sport that they are seriously considering Villa as an option after his name was discussed during talks about Rogers. Alejandro Garnacho has also been linked with Villa, but the Argentinian is said to be prioritising a move to Italy.

KIERAN GILL

West Ham mulling over Roma's Summerville bid

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign winger Crysencio Summerville.

As reported yesterday, Roma's latest bid of £39million plus add ons is a marginal increase and restructure on their second bid which was rejected.

Aston Villa have also been monitoring developments on the 24-year-old.

Roma are awaiting a reply from West Ham on their latest efforts to sign Crysencio Summerville

West Ham have enquired about Cardiff defender Dylan Lawlor.

Ipswich seal deal for new goalkeeper

Ipswich have completed the signing of goalkeeper Kayne van Oevelen from Volendam.

The fee is £4.25m with an initial £3.4m followed by £850,000 in add-ons.

The 22-year-old, who is seen as one for the future, has signed until 2031.

Ipswich have had a bid rejected for another goalkeeper, Kjell Scherpen from Union Saint-Gilloise.

As reported on Window Watch yesterday, Ipswich are close to sealing a £20m deal for Leicester City winger Abdul Fatawu with a further £3m in add-ons.

Ipswich are overhauling their goalkeeping department and discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop (right)

They are discussing an £8.5m deal for Fulham's Issa Diop and are negotiating with Celtic for versatile forward Daizen Maeda and free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita who is leaving Sporting Lisbon and had been close to joining Leeds United.

QPR snap up Lamptey

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal.

The 25-year-old has signed on a free transfer after leaving Serie A side Fiorentina.

Lamptey said: 'I like to get up and down, a lot of energy, a lot of fun. Hopefully I'll keep the fans on the edge of their seats.

Former Chelsea and Brighton full-back Tariq Lamptey has joined QPR on a permanent deal

'I'm tough tackling, I love one-v-ones, defensive and attacking, I just love playing the game.'

Lamptey's Fiorentina contract was terminated by mutual consent in May after the full-back ruptured his cruciate just three weeks after joining the Italian side from Brighton.

Fiorentina paid £6m for the Ghanaian.

Sheffield United weigh up Matondo move

Sheffield United are continuing to evaluate winger Rabbi Matondo who has impressed during their training camp in Valencia.

The Wales international, who is free to leave SK Brann, is due to play in a behind closed doors friendly against Huddersfield Town today.

Matondo figured in the Blades friendly against Levante last week and Chris Wilder is expected to make a decision this week with the likes of Derby County and Middlesbrough also showing interest.

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo

Sheffield Wednesday close in on TENTH summer signing

Aston Villa forward Tommi O'Reilly is poised to become Sheffield Wednesday's 10th summer signing.

The 22-year-old, who impressed on loan at Crewe in League Two last season, is due to sign on loan again at Wednesday.

The Owls' young goalkeeper Logan Stretch, 19, has been loaned out to National League North side Buxton, who are managed by former Wednesday youth coach Jordan Broadbent.

Man City teenager joins Northampton

Manchester City striker Matty Warhurst has joined Northampton Town.

The prolific 19-year-old was keen to leave for first team football and had interest from a host of clubs in League One and League Two including Stockport County, Cambridge United, Leyton Orient and Swindon Town.

Warhurst, who turns 20 in September, has scored 61 goals in 97 games for various City sides in the last few seasons, including 36 goals in 41 games for the under-18s before adding 13 goals in 18 Premier League 2 appearances and eight goals in 11 FA Youth Cup games.

Alex Scott turns down new Bournemouth deal

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract.

Scott has two years remaining on his current deal and was offered fresh terms by the Cherries in March this year.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United all hold an interest in the 22-year-old, but Bournemouth's stance is that he is not for sale this summer - regardless of his contract situation.

Daily Mail Sport understands Bournemouth have not put a price or valuation on the Under-21 European Championship winner as they do not consider him for sale.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has turned down a new contract at the club

Just last week, new Cherries boss Marco Rose told the media he was confident that in-demand Scott and Junior Kroupi would remain on the South Coast for their Europa League campaign.

Bournemouth's policy this summer is to keep hold of their best players for Europe - including Scott, Kroupi and winger Rayan - but it remains to be seen if substantial offers would test their resolve.

Scott played 39 times for Bournemouth last season and was key to securing European football for the first time in the club's history.

Thomas Tuchel awarded Scott his first international call-up last November, although he did not earn a cap.

The midfielder also travelled to the United States with the Three Lions before the World Cup to take part in their tournament preparation camp.

Even if Bournemouth could be persuaded to do business over Scott, it's understood that United would have to sell players to afford the £80m it would be likely to cost to prise him away from the Vitality Stadium.

The club want to sell top-earner Marcus Rashford following his loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa, and would listen to offers for Joshua Zirkzee. Manuel Ugarte would also have been available, but the Uruguay midfielder sustained a serious knee injury at the World Cup and will spend much of next season recuperating at Carrington.

As it stands, United will struggle to sign Scott and Roma midfielder Manu Kone appears to be a more realistic option after United held talks with the Frenchman's camp.

BOBBY MANZI AND CHRIS WHEELER

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola admits to TWO areas of concern in his Liverpool squad as he pushes board for more signings
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has identified two areas of concern and has issued an indirect appeal to transfer chiefs to kick on with summer plans.

The Reds have had a slow window thus far with only one arrival in Spanish World Cup winner Victor Munoz from Osasuna.

But Iraola issued a hands-off warning for Alisson and Alexis Mac Allister, who have been tracked by foreign clubs, and insisted he wants to add to his squad.

'It is difficult to say a number when the market is open,' said the Basque. 'You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

'There are obvious situations where we know we need to sign players. Winger, for example. We definitely need to sign a winger. In other situations, we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what the cost is, how we see the players we have.

'We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust that are not in the ideal situation. It depends on a lot of things.'

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has expressed two areas of concern since taking the job

Reds right back Conor Bradley is still out for several months due to a long-term knee injury

Iraola also said Liverpool are 'very thin' in terms of defensive depth, with Conor Bradley out for several months more yet after a long-term knee injury.

Asked about potential exits, Iraola insisted Alisson will remain No 1 after intense interest from Juventus earlier in the window and added on World Cup runner-up Mac Allister: 'Alexis has been one of the best players of the club in the last years.

'He has had a very good World Cup so it is normal that other clubs want our best players. It always happens in the market. I want to keep my good players. I am looking more to sign new players than losing the ones we have.'

Liverpool are in Chicago for a pre-season training camp and will fly to Nashville at the weekend for a friendly against Sunderland before warm-up games against Wrexham in New York City and Sunderland back here in the so-called Windy City.

Several star names are missing from the tour given their participation in the World Cup but Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Ryan Gravenberch will fly out to the States next week, likely in situ for the friendly at Yankee Stadium.

Captain Virgil van Dijk will not partake in the tour due to the fact he is 35 and had an arduous season last time. Since June 2025, he has played more minutes for club and country than any other player in Europe's top five leagues.

His compatriot Cody Gakpo will also be absent on compassionate leave after his partner lost a child during pregnancy last month. Alisson, now 33, is also not expected to join up with the squad after his exploits in the World Cup with Brazil.

Five players on tour are carrying injuries. Two, Wataru Endo and Stefan Bajcetic, will start training in the coming days. Giovanni Leoni is the closest of the other three, with Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike still 'some months' away from fitness.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes transfer update as £70m deal signed
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes transfer update as £70m deal signed

A huge update has emerged regarding Bruno Guimaraes' move to Arsenal

View 2 Images Newcastle United midfielder has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

Arsenal are ramping up their transfer activity following the conclusion of the World Cup. For all the talk at the end of last season of Mikel Arteta being handed another £250million war chest to bolster his squad this summer, the 2025/26 Premier League champions have been relatively quiet compared to their rivals.

‌



They kicked off the transfer window by sealing the permanent transfer of Piero Hincapie for £34m last month, before adding back-up goalkeeper Illan Meslier on a free transfer. Sporting director Andrea Berta has also addressed the much talked about left wing position, sanctioning the £17m departure of Leandro Trossard before acquiring his replacement - £34m Club Brugge winger Christos Tzolis - who is expected to formally sign this week.

‌



However, there is a growing sense of concern among the Arsenal faithful that Berta has still fallen short of their objectives so far in the window. The north Londoners are yet to offload several players surplus to requirements, including Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus and Christian Norgaard.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

More importantly, they are yet to bring in a marquee forward, a midfielder and a defender of starting calibre. Having already missed out on wonderkid Jeremy Monga to Manchester City, Berta’s dawdling also appears to have cost them the signature of Morgan Rogers.

Despite agreeing terms with the player, Arsenal refused to meet Aston Villa’s valuation of Rogers and Chelsea have since swept in and agreed a £117m move. Now, Mirror Football takes a look at two of the latest transfer developments involving the English champions.

‌



Bruno Guimaraes update

Newcastle sources have denied reports claiming they have opened talks with Arsenal over Bruno Guimaraes. It was reported by The Times on Tuesday that Arsenal had officially opened talks for the Brazilian midfielder, with Newcastle said to value him at £75m.

However, football.london cites Magpies sources as saying there still remains no bid, offers or even direct contact between themselves and Arsenal over the player. Discussions have taken place behind the scenes through intermediaries, with super agent Kia Joorabchian involved in helping sort out Guimaraes’ future.

The 28-year-old is also understood to have told Newcastle he wants to leave in order to win silverware elsewhere, with N5 being the most likely destination. But Arsenal’s valuation of Guimaraes, whose contract expires in less than two years, is said to be far lower than that of Newcastle's.

‌



£70m Emirates extension signed

View 2 Images Arsenal have been sponsored by Emirates since 2006 (Image: Phil Cole/Getty Images)

Arsenal have agreed a new deal with long-term title sponsor Emirates worth a reported £70m-a-year plus bonuses. The deal, negotiated by the club’s chief commercial officer Juliet Slot, who is set to become the latest executive to leave the club later this year, represents a huge increase on the £45m-a-year deal which ran until 2028.

It extends the airline’s long association with the north London club ahead of the current agreement’s scheduled expiry in 2028. The Telegraph reports that the renewed partnership covers the naming rights to Emirates Stadium and front-of-shirt sponsors for Arsenal’s men’s and women’s teams.

Article continues below

The stadium has borne the name of the United Arab Emirates’ airline since it was opened in 2006, with the shirt deal beginning at the same time. The improved terms are a result of Arteta’s side clinching their first Premier League title in 22 years and Arsenal Women’s Champions League success last year boosting the club’s commercial appeal.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers fires brutal dig at Arsenal as £117m Chelsea transfer confirmed
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers fires brutal dig at Arsenal as £117m Chelsea transfer confirmed

Morgan Rogers has officially been announced as a Chelsea player after a £117m move from Aston Villa and he has already spoken out after completing his move to Stamford Bridge

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers has finally completed his move to Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Morgan Rogers has hailed Chelsea as ‘the biggest club in London’ after Arsenal missed out on the England star. The Aston Villa midfielder was initially linked with a switch to the Emirates after his fine form in the Midlands.

‌



But Chelsea managed to hijack the move, sealing his services for £117m. Rogers was officially unveiled on Tuesday evening after undergoing a medical with his new employers.

‌



Speaking after his move was confirmed, he hailed Chelsea as the biggest club in the capital. The England star said: "I'm so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

‌



"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here and I can't wait to get started."

Chelsea to announce £34m transfer after Jude Bellingham World Cup slap READ MORE :

Chelsea could ruin Arsenal transfer plans AGAIN as Blues target John Stones READ MORE :

Rogers, 23, has joined Chelsea after a stunning season in which he scored 14 goals for Aston Villa and helped the side to the Europa League title.

In explaining why he chose to join the Blues, Rogers confirmed that new boss Xabi Alonso was a big influence, He said: “I’ve had a few conversations with him and I think it’s important for me to be here that I need to understand what the manager’s like, how he is and how he wants to operate.

‌



“It very much fits with the way I see the game, the way I want to play, and the way I want to be me, and be free and express myself. Him being a part of that was a massive factor in me being here.”

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers has suggested that Xabi Alonso was a big reason behind his move to Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Rogers will also link up with childhood friend Cole Palmer at Stamford Bridge, the pair having grown up together at Manchester City.

Article continues below

Speaking about his reunion with the playmaker, he added: “I’ve known Cole since I was about 14, first in the England [youth] teams and then when we were both at Man City together. We’ve been speaking about this for a while; we always would love to have played together. So, for it to happen, we’re both excited.

“He’s non-stop ringing my phone, texting me, and I can’t wait. I think that’s probably the most special thing, playing with one of your best friends and being around him every day. It’s something I’m really excited about.”

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho set to swap places with Morgan Rogers as Aston Villa eye swoop
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho set to swap places with Morgan Rogers as Aston Villa eye swoop

Chelsea have completed a £117m deal for Aston Villa and England star Morgan Rogers with former Manchester United man Alejandro Garnacho expected to go the other way to the Midlands

View 2 Images Chelsea are happy to let Garnacho leave (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea are set to get their wish for Alejandro Garnacho, with Aston Villa interested in signing the forward. The Blues only signed the Argentine frontman from Manchester United last summer in a £40m deal.

‌



But with Chelsea completing a £117m move for Villa and England star Morgan Rogers, the Blues are now happy to cut Garnacho adrift.

‌



Villa have already submitted a loan offer for him, with a conditional buy obligation attached and are close to finding an agreement. Chelsea initially wanted a permanent deal for the Argentine.

‌



Unai Emery is thought to be a big fan of Garnacho and is hoping to play a role in a career revival. Villa’s interest comes just days after new boss Xabi Alonso admitted that he was happy to let the forward leave.

He said: "Well the situation is that we have spoken with the sporting directors. There is an interest for him [Garnacho] from other clubs. So let's see how this develops. But hopefully, it finishes in the best possible way for other clubs."

West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest READ MORE :

Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection READ MORE :

Garnacho, 22, signed a seven-year deal with Chelsea last summer following his arrival from Old Trafford. He made 43 appearances across his debut season, scoring just eight goals, only one of which came in the Premier League.

‌



Garnacho would arrive at Villa as Rogers’ replacement following his own move to Chelsea. The former Middlesbrough man scored 14 times last term but Paul Merson is not convinced his move to West London is the right one.

He said: “It's a lot of money. Crazy money. Bringing Morgan Rogers in for £117m isn't what Chelsea needed.

“They've got Cole Palmer! They play in the same position! Rogers went to the World Cup instead of Palmer, because they play in the same position.

‌



View 2 Images Garnacho only joined Chelsea last summer (Image: Getty Images)

“Unless Chelsea go for the almighty and sell Enzo Fernandez - and swallow the pill for him, because he's not worth £100m - and then play Moises Caicedo at the base, then Rogers and Palmer both ahead of him.”

He continued: “Rogers has got to carry that price tag around with him. He will sit there and say: 'there is no pressure on me, I didn't pay that fee'. But it's a load of rubbish. Everybody will look at that when you don't do well.

‌



“A lot of people were saying it was too much for Declan Rice and Moises Caicedo when they moved for £100m. But the biggest compliment I can give them is nobody ever mentions it. They were good signings. That's what Rogers has got to hope for.

“But he's got to make things happen, which is a harder position to be in than Rice and Caicedo were. In midfield, you can do this and that - but Rogers will be judged on scoring and creating goals. That's the hardest job in the world.

“I'm also sure that at the start of last season, he was atrocious for Aston Villa. I'm sure he was. Then he came good and then had a good second part of the season.

Article continues below

“He can't play like that at Chelsea. That is an absolute no-go, it's a different ball game when you go for that kind of money.”

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers completes record-breaking £117m transfer to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers completes record-breaking £117m transfer to Chelsea

Chelsea have completed the capture of Morgan Rogers after beating Arsenal to a whopping £117million deal for one of England's World Cup stars

View 2 Images Rogers has put pen to paper on a seven-year deal at Stamford Bridge (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Morgan Rogers is officially a Chelsea player after finalising a transfer from Aston Villa which makes him the most expensive British footballer in history.

‌



The England star, 23, has put pen to paper on a contract until 2033 which includes an option for a further year. He moves to Stamford Bridge for a seismic £117million transfer fee, a figure which eclipses the amount Manchester City agreed to part with in order to acquire his World Cup team-mate, Elliot Anderson.

‌



Rogers was pursued for over two years by Chelsea, who beat off competition from Arsenal to sign the versatile attacking midfielder.

‌



Chelsea stole a march on Arsenal when the Gunners were unwilling to move from their valuation of the player, Mirror Football understands.

According to sources, the Gunners valued the England international at £80m, and were willing to pay a slight premium - but were left stunned when Chelsea agreed to pay a fee that makes Rogers' move the most expensive transfer of an Englishman in history - beating Anderson's move from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City by £1m.

West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest READ MORE :

His capture is a first major win for the Blues' new manager, Xabi Alonso, who held productive talks with Rogers to help entice the former Middlesbrough man to west London.

‌



Upon finalising his move, Rogers said: "I'm so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here and I can't wait to get started.

“I’ve had a few conversations with him [Alonso] and I think it’s important for me to be here that I need to understand what the manager’s like, how he is and how he wants to operate.

‌



“It very much fits with the way I see the game, the way I want to play, and the way I want to be me, and be free and express myself. Him being a part of that was a massive factor in me being here.”

View 2 Images Rogers with new boss Xabi Alonso (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Rogers came through the youth academy at West Brom before moving to Man City in 2019. He didn't make a first-team appearance for City and went out on loan to Lincoln, Bournemouth and Blackpool.

‌



He joined Middlesbrough for an undisclosed fee in 2023 scoring five times in their run to the League Cup semi-finals. He joined Villa in the following January for £8m, potentially rising to £15m.

In all, Rogers made 125 appearances for Villa scoring 31 goals and helping them to the Europa League title last term.

On the international stage, Rogers made his senior England debut in November 2004 in a 3-0 victory against Greece in Athens. He has played 22 times for England, including at the recent World Cup, scoring once.

‌



The five-year-old daughter of New Bay opened her account just over a year ago at the Surrey track over the same trip and similar fast ground, before scoring again a month later on the Wolverhampton all-weather.

‌



Daniel and Claire Kubler’s mare scored a third career victory at Newcastle in March and more recently was unlucky in running back here in May, when unable to find an opening entering the final furlong before being switched to make a run.

Under top weight she finished like a train to go down by a neck and a head behind Summer Heat and Land Of Magic, with form of that race working out really well.

If Rob Hornby’s mount can dictate terms from the front he will be tough to beat for a yard in great form.

Sports.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi 'reaches transfer agreement' after Man City, Man Utd and Arsenal interest
Sports.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi 'reaches transfer agreement' after Man City, Man Utd and Arsenal interest

The Lille and Morocco midfielder is one of the most sought-after talents in Europe, with several Premier League clubs having been keeping a close eye on his situation

View 2 Images There is Premier League interest in Lille and Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Manchester City have reportedly reached an initial agreement with Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi over personal terms as they work on the transfer. Manchester United and Arsenal have both also been linked with the Morocco international.

‌



The 18-year-old is one of the most highly-rated talents in Europe, with teams queuing up to try and sign him this summer. He also caught the eye while representing Morocco in the World Cup.

‌



Despite his young age, Bouaddi played 42 times in all competitions for Lille last season and has become a key player for the Ligue 1 side. It’s reported that they will demand around €100 million (£85m) to sell him.

‌



Rayan Cherki singles out Didier Deschamps after backlash to England incident and 'snub' READ MORE :

Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection READ MORE :

Speaking earlier this month, Lille chairman Oliver Letang hinted at the price he wants. “When I see [Elliot] Anderson move to Manchester City for £116 million and [Sandro] Tonali to Tottenham for £100 million, and they don’t have the potential for development that Ayyoub has because he possesses unique qualities.

“I have a price in mind, and we’ll see what happens."

According to journalist Nicolo Schira, City have agreed a contract with the teenager that runs until 2031. The club will now continue talks with Lille to try and reach a club-to-club agreement over the transfer fee.

‌



It’s added that City expect two other ‘top European clubs’ to make a move, although it’s not said who those clubs are. Arsenal and United are two other clubs who have been heavily linked with an interest.

View 2 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi impressed for Morocco at this summer's World Cup (Image: Sathire Kelpa/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Reports suggest that City see Bouaddi as someone who can go straight into Enzo Maresca’s starting line-up , despite the £116 million signing of England star Anderson earlier in the window. That may have given them the edge over some of their rivals.

‌



Former France international Emmanuel Petit has been full of praise about Bouaddi. "He's been one of the strongest young players in France,” he told talkSPORT

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"We've seen that against Brazil. He's shown maturity and personality.

‌



"Even at the end of the game, I saw him try to dribble in his own penalty area. The confidence, he's got quality, he's got physical presence, he's got the tactical knowledge, he's got the technical skills.

"I'm not surprised at all that he's been targeted for two seasons now with the big clubs in Europe, and it will be a fierce battle to get him."

Sports.title: West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest
Sports.content:
West Ham strike £68m deal to sell Crysencio Summerville amid Man Utd interest

Manchester United were among the clubs linked with a move for West Ham winger Crysencio Summerville but it appears that the Dutchman is set to move elsewhere

View 2 Images Summerville is set to leave West Ham after two years (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to lose out on Crysencio Summerville, with the West Ham star on the verge of a move to Saudi Arabia. The Red Devils were linked with a swoop for the Dutchman this summer, following the Hammers’ relegation from the Premier League.

‌



They were interested in him alongside Mateus Fernandes, who eventually completed a big-money move to Tottenham Hotspur. But United are also set to be frustrated in their pursuit of the former Leeds man.

‌



The Londoners have agreed a £68m deal with Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal. Italian giants Roma were also interested but were only willing to offer around £39m.

‌



Summerville, who scored five Premier League goals last term, is now expected to undergo a medical ahead of completing his switch to the Middle East. West Ham in the meantime will aim to re-invest the considerable fee as they attempt to earn promotion from the Championship at the first time of asking.

The only signing that the Hammers have made so far is a deal for Venezuelan international Keiber Lamadrid. But one considerable boost has been Jarrod Bowen’s decision to commit his future to the club.

FSG confirm Liverpool sale talks as billionaire family eyes deal after resignation READ MORE :

Man City to sign youngster from under Arsenal's noses after contract rejection READ MORE :

Speaking at the time, he said: "My main motivation is staying and bringing this club back to the Premier League where we belong. It was only right for me to speak at the right time. Ultimately it [relegation] hurt everyone and it should hurt everyone.

‌



"I flew out to Prague to meet (club directors) Daniel [Kretinsky] and Jiri [Svarc] and the ambition that I got from them, certainly in terms of the direction the club wants to move in, it interests me a lot. It didn't take a lot, because this club means a lot to me.

"For me, when you're here for a longer amount of time, you gain more affection, you grow into the club more, you grow into your role more and more, and I think that's what I've done.

View 2 Images Crysencio Summerville is expected to move to Saudi Arabia (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I've been here six and a half years and transitioned from a boy to a man and I've never tried to hide away from anything.

"There are things you can do better, but certainly in my character on the pitch and off the pitch, I never try and hide away from anything and shift the blame.

"I always try and stand up for them and just kind of live my life as captain of West Ham and also as a fan as well.

Article continues below

"I see myself in years to come as a West Ham fan. So, I always think 'what would they want as a fan if they got the opportunity to play on the pitch?'. For me, I think I'm like that character as well, so I think that's the way."

Sports.title: Sepp Blatter blasts FIFA and Gianni Infantino and says World Cup 'lost its credibility'
Sports.content:
Sepp Blatter blasts FIFA and Gianni Infantino and says World Cup 'lost its credibility'

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has faced severe criticism during the World Cup for his close relationship with US President Donald Trump with controversial former chief Sepp Blatter among those to speak out

View 2 Images Sepp Blatter has taken a fresh swipe at Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

Sepp Blatter has once again called for ‘new leadership’ at FIFA in a brutal dig at Gianni Infantino. The current president has faced serious criticism for a number of decisions throughout this summer’s World Cup.

‌



Ticket prices, over-commercialisation, as well as his close relationship with US President Donald Trump have all been issues. Criticism then sharply increased after the decision to suspend Folarin Balogun’s red card following a phone call from Trump.

‌



Blatter tore into Infantino immediately after that decision. Taking to Twitter, he said: “Red cards are not overturned by political phone calls. They are overturned by rules, evidence and independent bodies.

‌



"If a U.S. President intervenes with the FIFA President — and a player is suddenly cleared before a World Cup knockout match — the question is unavoidable: Quo vadis, FIFA? Quo vadis means 'Where are you going?' in Latin. Football must never become a playground for political power.”

Blatter has now doubled down with a fresh post calling for change right at the top of the organisation just days after the World Cup final.

Lionel Messi sparks conspiracy theories as footage from World Cup final speech leaked READ MORE :

He said: “The longest World Cup has come to an end - with the right champions. But on the way to the final whistle, the tournament had lost its credibility. Politics must not be allowed to overshadow the game. Now it is up to the fans, players and national associations to reclaim football and bring it back to its roots under new leadership.”

‌



While Blatter has called for fresh leadership, it appears that is unlikely. La Liga president Javier Tebas has claimed that due to a lack of opposition, it appears that Infantino is set to stay in charge.

Asked if he should quit, Tebas replied: "In my opinion, yes, I think his time is up." He added: "There's no opposition candidate, nobody wants to stand just to lose. He shouldn't stay, but the current state of affairs means he won't leave.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has faced plenty of criticism throughout the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"These past few days here in America, I've heard many people who are against Infantino, who disagree with what he's doing,

"They say it, but then they do nothing. I don't know what's worse, the silence or the complicity, because those who stay silent are perfectly aware of the damage football is suffering.

"The suspension of the American player's ban was absolutely serious. They were lucky that Belgium eliminated the USA, because otherwise a case could have arisen that might have cost Infantino his job. Since Belgium won, they managed to bury the matter. But these things are just the tip of the iceberg."
